Fuguo Gong Yun'e; Prince Luyi Yunyou; Prince Yixian Yinxiang.
3
恂勤郡王允禵愉恪郡王允潖果毅親王允禮
Prince Xunqin of the Second Rank Yinti; Prince Yukuo of the Second Rank Yunpeng; Prince Guoyi Yunli.

果恭郡王弘適簡靖貝勒允禕慎靖郡王允禧
Prince Guogong of the Second Rank Hongshi; Beile Jianjing Yunyi; Prince Shenjing of the Second Rank Yunxi.

質莊親王永瑢恭勤貝勒允祜郡王品級誠貝勒允祁
Prince Zhizhuang Yongrong; Beile Gongqin Yunhu; Beile Cheng Yunqi, of princely rank.

Prince Xianke Yunbi.

端親王弘暉和恭親王弘晝懷親王福惠
Prince Duan Honghui; Prince Hegong Hongzhou; Prince Huai Fuhui.
8
聖祖三十五子：孝誠仁皇后生承祜、理密親王允礽，孝恭仁皇后生第六子允祚、世宗、恂勤郡王允禵，敬敏皇貴妃章佳氏生怡賢親王允祥，溫僖貴妃鈕祜祿氏生貝子品級允䄉，順懿密妃王氏生愉恪郡王允潖、莊恪親王允祿、第十八子允祄，純裕勤妃陳氏生果毅親王允禮，惠妃納喇氏生承慶、貝子品級允禔，宜妃郭絡羅氏生恒溫親王允祺、第九子允禟、第十一子允禌，榮妃馬佳氏生承瑞、賽音察渾、長華、長生、誠隱郡王允祉，成妃戴佳氏生淳度，良妃衛氏生第八子允禩，定妃萬琉哈氏生履懿親王允祹，平妃赫舍里氏生允禨，通嬪納喇氏生萬黼、允禶，襄嬪高氏生第十九子允禝、簡靖貝勒允禕，謹嬪色赫圖氏生恭勤貝勒允祜，靜嬪石氏生郡王品級誠貝勒允祁，熙嬪陳氏生慎靖郡王允禧，穆嬪陳氏生諴恪親王允祕，貴人郭絡羅氏生允䄔，貴人陳氏生允禐。 允祿出為承澤裕親王碩塞後，允祚、允禌、允祄、允禝皆殤，無封。 承瑞、承祜、承慶、賽音察渾、長華、長生、萬黼、允禶，允騕、允禨、允禐皆殤，不齒序。
Kangxi had thirty-five sons. Empress Xiaochengren gave birth to Chenghu and Prince Mizhi Yinreng. Empress Xiaogongren gave birth to the sixth son Yunzuo, the future Yongzheng Emperor, and Prince Xunqin Yinti. Imperial Noble Consort Jingmin, née Zhang, gave birth to Prince Yixian Yinxiang. Consort Wenxi, née Niuhuru, gave birth to Yun'e, who held beizi rank. Consort Shunyi, née Wang, gave birth to Prince Yukuo Yunpeng, Prince Zhuangke Yunlu, and the eighteenth son Yunxu. Consort Chunyu, née Chen, gave birth to Prince Guoyi Yunli. Consort Hui, née Nara, gave birth to Chengqing and Yunzhi, who held beizi rank. Consort Yi, née Guoluoluo, gave birth to Prince Hengwen Yunqi, the ninth son Yuntang, and the eleventh son Yunli. Consort Rong, née Ma, gave birth to Chengrui, Saiyinchahun, Changhua, Changsheng, and Prince Chengyin Yinzhi. Consort Cheng, née Dai, gave birth to Chundu. Consort Liang, née Wei, gave birth to the eighth son Yunsi. Consort Ding, née Wanliuha, gave birth to Prince Luyi Yunyou. Consort Ping, née Hesheri, gave birth to Yunxi. Lady Tong, née Nara, gave birth to Wanfu and Yun'e. Lady Xiang, née Gao, gave birth to the nineteenth son and Beile Jianjing Yunyi. Lady Jin, née Sehetu, gave birth to Beile Gongqin Yunhu. Lady Jing, née Shi, gave birth to Beile Cheng Yunqi, of princely rank. Lady Xi, née Chen, gave birth to Prince Shenjing Yunxi. Lady Mu, née Chen, gave birth to Prince Xianke Yunbi. A lady of the Guo clan gave birth to Yun'e; a lady of the Chen clan gave birth to Yunxu. Yunlu was adopted as heir to Prince Chengyu Shuo Sai. Yunzuo, Yunli, Yunxu, and the nineteenth son all died in infancy and were never enfeoffed. Chengrui, Chenghu, Chengqing, Saiyinchahun, Changhua, Changsheng, Wanfu, Yun'e, Yunjiao, Yunxi, and Yunxu likewise died young and were not numbered among the sons in the succession.
9
固山貝子品級允禔，聖祖第一子。 上有巡幸，輒從。 康熙二十九年，命副裕親王福全禦噶爾丹。 上以允禔聽讒，與福全不協，私自陳奏，慮在軍中僨事，召還京師。 未幾，福全師還，命諸王大臣勘鞫。 福全初欲發允禔在軍中過失，會有嚴旨，戒允禔不得與福全異同，福全乃引罪。 語在福全傳。
Yunzhi, who held the rank of gushan beizi, was Kangxi's eldest son. Whenever the emperor traveled, he went along. In the twenty-ninth year of the Kangxi reign he was ordered to serve as deputy to Prince Yu Fucan in operations against Galdan. The emperor found that Yunzhi listened to slander, clashed with Fucan, and sent private memorials; fearing discord in the army, he recalled Yunzhi to the capital. Soon afterward Fucan's army returned, and the emperor ordered the princes and senior ministers to investigate and adjudicate the matter. Fucan had at first intended to expose Yunzhi's misconduct in the field, but a stern edict warned Yunzhi not to oppose Fucan in any way, whereupon Fucan accepted guilt himself. This is recounted in the biography of Fucan.
10
三十五年，從上征噶爾丹，命與內大臣索額圖統先發八旗前鋒、漢軍火器營與四旗察哈爾及綠旗諸軍駐拖陵布喇克待上。 西路大將軍費揚古軍後期，下軍中大臣議，亦遣官諮允禔。 上遂進軍昭莫多。 既捷，允禔留中拖陵犒軍，尋召還。
In the thirty-fifth year he accompanied the emperor on the campaign against Galdan and was ordered, with Inner Minister Songgotu, to lead the advance forces—the Eight Banner vanguard, the Han Army firearms battalion, four Chahar banners, and the Green Standard troops—and to encamp at Tuolingbulake until the emperor arrived. When Commander-in-Chief Fei Yanggu on the western route fell behind schedule, the case was submitted to the army's senior ministers for deliberation, and envoys were also sent to seek Yunzhi's opinion. The emperor then marched on Jao Modo. After the victory Yunzhi stayed at Tuoling to distribute rewards to the army and was soon recalled.
11
三十七年三月，封直郡王。
In the third month of the thirty-seventh year he was created Prince Zhi of the Second Rank.
12
三十九年四月，上巡視永定河堤，鳩工疏濬，命允禔總之。
In the fourth month of the thirty-ninth year the emperor inspected the Yongding River dikes, organized labor to dredge them, and put Yunzhi in overall charge.
13
四十七年九月，皇太子允礽既廢，允禔奏曰：「允礽所行卑汙，失人心。 術士張明德嘗相允禩必大貴。 如誅允礽，不必出皇父手。 」上怒，詔斥允禔凶頑愚昧，並戒諸皇子勿縱屬下人生事。 允禔用喇嘛巴漢格隆魘術魘廢太子，事發，上命監守。 尋奪爵，幽於第。 四月，上將巡塞外，諭：「允禔鎮魘皇太子及諸皇子，不念父母兄弟，事無顧忌。 萬一禍發，朕在塞外，三日後始聞，何由制止？ 」下諸王大臣議，於八旗遣護軍參領八、護軍校八、護軍八十，仍於允禔府中監守。 上復遣貝勒延壽，貝子蘇努，公鄂飛，都統辛泰，護軍統領圖爾海、陳泰，並八旗章京十七人，更番監守，仍嚴諭疏忽當族誅。
In the ninth month of the forty-seventh year, after Crown Prince Yinreng had been deposed, Yunzhi memorialized: "Yinreng's conduct is base and shameful and has lost him the people's regard. The diviner Zhang Mingde had once read Yunsi's features and declared that he was destined for great eminence. If Yinreng is to be put to death, it need not be by the Emperor Father's own hand." The emperor was furious. An edict denounced Yunzhi as vicious, stubborn, and foolish, and warned all the princes not to let their followers make trouble. Yunzhi had used the Lama Bahangelong's sorcery to curse the crown prince; when the plot was exposed the emperor ordered him placed under guard. Soon afterward his title was revoked and he was confined to his mansion. In the fourth month, as the emperor was about to tour the frontier, he said: "Yunzhi has used sorcery against the crown prince and the other princes. He gives no thought to parents or brothers and acts without restraint. If trouble should break out while I am beyond the passes, I would not hear of it for three days—how could it be stopped?" The matter was referred to the princes and senior ministers. From the Eight Banners eight guard company commanders, eight guard lieutenants, and eighty guards were sent to keep watch in Yunzhi's mansion. The emperor also sent Beile Yanshou, Beizi Sunu, Duke Efei, Banner General Xintai, Guard Commanders Tu'erhai and Chentai, and seventeen clerks from the Eight Banners to relieve one another in guarding him, with a stern warning that anyone negligent would bring extinction upon his clan.
14
雍正十二年，卒，世宗命以固山貝子禮殯葬。 子弘昉，襲鎮國公。 卒。 子永揚，襲輔國公。 坐事，奪爵。 高宗以允禔第十三子弘晌封奉恩將軍，世襲。
In the twelfth year of the Yongzheng reign he died, and the Yongzheng Emperor ordered him buried with the rites due a gushan beizi. His son Hongfang inherited the title of Duke of the State Supporting the Nation. He died. His son Yongyang inherited the title of Duke of the State Assisting the Nation. He was convicted in a case and stripped of his title. The Qianlong Emperor enfeoffed Yunzhi's thirteenth son Hongshang as General by Grace, with the title to pass in perpetuity.
15
理密親王允礽，聖祖第二子。 康熙十四年十二月乙丑，聖祖以太皇太后、皇太后命立為皇太子。 太子方幼，上親教之讀書。 六歲就傅，令大學士張英、李光地為之師，又命大學士熊賜履授以性理諸書。
Prince Mizhi Yinreng was Kangxi's second son. On yichou in the twelfth month of the fourteenth year of the Kangxi reign, Kangxi, acting on the command of the Grand Empress Dowager and the Empress Dowager, installed him as crown prince. While the crown prince was still young, the emperor personally taught him to read. At the age of six he was given tutors. The emperor appointed Grand Secretaries Zhang Ying and Li Guangdi as his teachers and ordered Grand Secretary Xiong Cilu to instruct him in Neo-Confucian texts.
16
二十五年，上召江寧巡撫湯斌，以禮部尚書領詹事。 斌薦起原任直隸大名道耿介為少詹事，輔導太子。 介旋以疾辭。 逾年，斌亦卒。 太子通滿、漢文字，嫻騎射，從上行幸，賡詠斐然。
In the twenty-fifth year the emperor summoned Jiangning Governor Tang Bin and appointed him Minister of Rites while also making him Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent. Tang Bin recommended the former Zhili Daming Circuit Intendant Geng Jie for recall and appointed him Junior Tutor to assist in guiding the crown prince. Geng Jie soon resigned, citing illness. The following year Tang Bin also died. The crown prince mastered Manchu and Chinese writing, was skilled in riding and archery, accompanied the emperor on his travels, and composed verse of notable elegance.
17
二十九年七月，上親征噶爾丹，駐蹕古魯富爾堅嘉渾噶山，遘疾，召太子及皇三子允祉至行宮。 太子侍疾無憂色，上不懌，遣太子先還。
In the seventh month of the twenty-ninth year the emperor led a campaign against Galdan and halted at Gurufurjianggahunga Mountain, where he fell ill and summoned the crown prince and the third prince Yinzhi to his traveling palace. The crown prince attended him without showing concern, which displeased the emperor, and he sent the crown prince back ahead of him.
18
三十三年，禮部奏祭奉先殿儀注，太子拜褥置檻內，上諭尚書沙穆哈移設檻外，沙穆哈請旨記檔，上命奪沙穆哈官。
In the thirty-third year the Ministry of Rites submitted the ritual for sacrifice at the Hall of Imperial Ancestors with the crown prince's kneeling mat placed inside the railing. The emperor instructed Minister Shamoha to move it outside. Shamoha asked that the order be entered in the record, and the emperor stripped him of office.
19
三十四年，冊石氏為太子妃。
In the thirty-fourth year Lady Shi was invested as the crown princess.
20
三十五年二月，上再親征噶爾丹，命太子代行郊祀禮； 各部院奏章，聽太子處理； 事重要，諸大臣議定，啟太子。 六月，上破噶爾丹，還，太子迎於諾海河朔，命太子先還。 上至京師，太子率群臣郊迎。 明年，上行兵寧夏，仍命太子居守。 有為蜚語聞上者，謂太子暱比匪人，素行遂變。 上還京師，錄太子左右用事者置於法。 自此眷愛漸替。
In the second month of the thirty-fifth year the emperor again led a campaign against Galdan and ordered the crown prince to perform the suburban sacrifices on his behalf; memorials from all boards and courts were to be handled by the crown prince; on important matters the senior ministers were to deliberate first and then report to the crown prince. In the sixth month the emperor defeated Galdan and returned. The crown prince met him north of the Nuo River, but the emperor ordered him to go back first. When the emperor reached the capital, the crown prince led the officials in a suburban welcome. The following year, when the emperor marched on Ningxia, he again left the crown prince in charge at the capital. Slander reached the emperor claiming that the crown prince kept company with worthless men and that his conduct had changed. When the emperor returned to the capital he arrested the crown prince's powerful associates and punished them according to law. From this point the emperor's affection for him gradually cooled.
21
四十七年八月，上行圍。 皇十八子允祄疾作，留永安拜昂阿。 上回鑾臨視，允祄病篤。 上諭曰：「允祄病無濟，區區稚子，有何關係？ 至於朕躬，上恐貽高年皇太后之憂，下則係天下臣民之望，宜割愛就道。 」因啟蹕。
In the eighth month of the forty-seventh year the emperor went on the autumn hunt. The eighteenth prince Yunxu fell ill and was left behind at Yong'an Bayang'a. The emperor turned back to visit him, but Yunxu's illness was already grave. The emperor said: "Yunxu's illness cannot be cured. He is only a small child—what does it matter? As for myself, above I would grieve the aged Grand Empress Dowager, and below the officials and people of the realm depend on me. I must set aside personal sorrow and continue on my way." He then resumed the imperial progress.
22
九月乙亥，次佈爾哈蘇台，召太子，集諸王大臣諭曰：「允礽不法祖德，不遵朕訓，暴戾淫亂，朕包容二十年矣。 乃其惡愈張，僇辱廷臣，專擅威權，鳩聚黨與，窺伺朕躬起居動作。 平郡王訥爾素、貝勒海善、公普奇遭其毆撻，大臣官員亦罹其毒。 朕巡幸陝西、江南、浙江，未嘗一事擾民。 允礽與所屬恣行乖戾，無所不至，遣使邀截蒙古貢使，攘進御之馬，致蒙古俱不心服。 朕以其賦性奢侈，用凌普為內務府總管，以為允礽乳母之夫，便其徵索。 凌普更為貪婪，包衣下人無不怨憾。 皇十八子抱病，諸臣以朕年高，無不為朕憂，允礽乃親兄，絕無友愛之意。 朕加以責讓，忿然發怒，每夜偪近布城，裂縫竊視。 從前索額圖欲謀大事，朕知而誅之，今允礽欲為復仇。 朕不卜今日被鴆、明日遇害，晝夜戒慎不寧。 似此不孝不仁，太祖、太宗、世祖所締造，朕所治平之天下，斷不可付此人！ 」上且諭且泣，至於僕地，即日執允礽，命直郡王允禔監之，誅索額圖二子格爾芬、阿爾吉善，及允礽左右二格、蘇爾特、哈什太、薩爾邦阿； 其罪稍減者，遣戍盛京。 次日，上命宣諭諸臣及侍衛官兵，略謂：「允礽為太子，有所使令，眾敢不從，即其中豈無奔走逢迎之人？ 今事內干連應誅者已誅，應遣者已遣，餘不更推求，毋危懼。 」
On yihai in the ninth month, while halted at Bu'erhasutai, he summoned the crown prince, assembled the princes and senior ministers, and declared: "Yinreng does not honor the virtue of our ancestors or heed my instruction. He is violent, cruel, and dissolute. I have borne with him for twenty years. Yet his wickedness has only grown. He insults court ministers, monopolizes power, gathers factions, and spies on my every movement. Prince Ping of the Second Rank Ne'ersu, Beile Haishan, and Duke Puqi have been beaten by him, and senior ministers and officials have likewise suffered at his hands. On my tours to Shaanxi, Jiangnan, and Zhejiang I never once troubled the people. Yinreng and his followers acted with unrestrained perversity in every regard. They sent agents to intercept Mongol tribute envoys, seized horses presented to the throne, and caused the Mongols to lose all respect. Knowing his extravagant nature, I appointed Ling Pu superintendent of the Imperial Household Department—he was the husband of Yinreng's wet nurse—so that Yinreng could more easily extort what he wanted. Ling Pu became even greedier, and every bondservant under him seethed with resentment. When the eighteenth prince fell ill, every minister, mindful of my advanced age, was anxious on my behalf, yet Yinreng, his own elder brother, showed not the slightest brotherly concern. When I reproached him he flew into a rage. Every night he crept close to the cloth partition around my quarters and peered through the cracks. Long ago Songgotu plotted treason; I discovered it and put him to death. Now Yinreng seeks revenge. I cannot know whether I shall be poisoned today or murdered tomorrow. Day and night I live in dread and cannot rest. A man so unfilial and cruel—the realm forged by Taizu, Taizong, and Shizu and brought to peace under my rule—must never be entrusted to such a person!" The emperor spoke through his tears until he collapsed prostrate. That same day Yinreng was seized and Prince Zhi Yunzhi was ordered to guard him. Songgotu's sons Ge'erfen and A'erjishan were executed, along with Yinreng's close attendants Erge, Su'erte, Hashitai, and Sa'erbang'a; those whose crimes were somewhat lighter were banished to garrison duty at Mukden. The next day the emperor ordered an announcement to the ministers and guard officers and troops, saying in substance: "As crown prince, Yinreng gave orders—who would have dared refuse? Surely some among you rushed to flatter him. Those implicated who deserved death have been put to death, and those who deserved banishment have been banished. The rest will not be pursued further. Do not be afraid." "
23
上既廢太子，憤懣不已，六夕不安寢，召扈從諸臣涕泣言之，諸臣皆嗚咽。 既又諭諸臣，謂：「觀允礽行事，與人大不同，類狂易之疾，似有鬼物憑之者。 」及還京，設氈帷上駟院側，令允礽居焉，更命皇四子與允禔同守之。 尋以廢太子詔宣示天下，上並親撰文告天​​地、太廟、社稷曰：「臣祗承丕緒，四十七年餘矣，於國計民生，夙夜兢業，無事不可質諸天地。 稽古史冊，興亡雖非一轍，而得深懼祖宗垂貽之大業自臣而隳，故身雖不德，而親握朝綱，一切政務，不徇偏私，不謀群小，事無久稽，悉由獨斷，亦惟鞠躬盡瘁，死而後已，在位一日，勤求治理，斷不敢少懈。 不知臣有何辜，生子如允礽者，不孝不義，暴虐慆淫，若非鬼物憑附，狂易成疾，有血氣者豈忍為之？ 允礽口不道忠信之言，身不履德義之行，咎戾多端，難以承祀，用是昭告昊天上帝，特行廢斥，勿致貽憂邦國，痛毒蒼生。 抑臣更有哀籥者，臣自幼而孤，未得親承父母之訓子，遠不及臣，如大清歷數綿長，延臣壽命，臣當益加勤勉，謹保終始； 如我國家無福，即殃及臣躬，以全臣令名。 臣不勝痛切，謹告。 」
After deposing the crown prince the emperor could not shake his anger and grief. For six nights he slept fitfully and summoned the ministers in his retinue, speaking through his tears; all of them sobbed. He then told the ministers again: "Judging from Yinreng's conduct, it is utterly unlike that of other men. It resembles mania, as though some evil spirit possessed him." When he returned to the capital he pitched a felt tent beside the Upper Stud Farm and had Yinreng live there, further ordering the fourth prince and Yunzhi to guard him jointly. Soon the edict deposing the crown prince was proclaimed throughout the realm. The emperor also personally composed a memorial reporting to Heaven and Earth, the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and the Altar of Land and Grain: "Your subject reverently received the great succession more than forty-seven years ago. In state affairs and the people's livelihood I have labored day and night, and in nothing have I failed to answer before Heaven and Earth. The histories show that rise and fall follow many paths, yet I have deeply feared that the great enterprise bequeathed by the ancestors might perish through me. Though lacking in personal virtue, I have held the reins of government myself. In all affairs of state I have refused partiality, refused to plot with petty men, allowed nothing to linger, and decided everything on my own. I have striven to exhaust myself in service until death, and for every day in office I have sought good governance without daring the slightest slackening. I know not what guilt your subject has committed to bear a son like Yinreng—unfilial, unjust, violent, and dissolute. Unless some evil spirit possessed him and mania took hold, what man of flesh and blood could bear to act thus? Yinreng's mouth speaks no word of loyalty or faith, and his person follows no path of virtue or righteousness. His crimes are many and he cannot inherit the sacrifices. Therefore I proclaim to the Supreme Lord of Vast Heaven and hereby depose him, lest he bring grief to the state and suffering to the people. Your subject has yet another sorrow. From childhood I was orphaned and never received my parents' instruction in raising a son—how far my son falls short of me. If the Qing dynasty's mandate is long and my life is prolonged, I shall redouble my diligence and guard my course to the end; but if our state lacks fortune, let the calamity fall on me alone, so that my good name may be preserved. Your subject is overcome with anguish and respectfully reports. "
24
太子既廢，上諭：「諸皇子中如有謀為皇太子者，即國之賊，法所不宥。 」諸皇子中皇八子允禩謀最力，上知之，命執付議政大臣議罪，削貝勒。 十月，皇三子允祉發喇嘛巴漢格隆，為皇長子允禔厭允礽事。 上令侍衛發允礽所居，得厭勝物十餘事。 上幸南苑行圍，遘疾，還宮，召允礽入見，使居咸安宮。 上逾諸近臣曰：「朕召見允礽，詢問前事，竟有全不知者，是其諸惡皆被魘魅而然。 果蒙天佑，狂疾頓除，改而為善，朕自有裁奪。 」廷臣希旨有請復立允礽為太子者，上不許。 左副都御史勞之辨奏上，上斥其奸詭，奪官，予杖。
After the crown prince was deposed the emperor declared: "Among the princes, whoever plots to become crown prince is a traitor to the state and will not be spared by law. Among the princes the eighth prince Yunsi plotted most vigorously. The emperor learned of it, ordered him seized and handed to the Deliberative Princes and Ministers for judgment, and stripped him of his beile title. In the tenth month the third prince Yinzhi exposed the Lama Bahangelong in the affair by which the eldest prince Yunzhi had used sorcery against Yinreng. The emperor ordered guards to search Yinreng's residence and found more than ten objects used for sorcery. The emperor went to the Southern Park for the hunt, fell ill, and returned to the palace. He summoned Yinreng for an audience and had him live in the Xian'an Palace. The emperor told his close ministers: "When I summoned Yinreng and questioned him about past affairs, he knew nothing at all. His every wicked act, it seems, was the work of sorcery. If Heaven truly blesses him and his madness is lifted so that he turns to goodness, I shall judge for myself." Reading the emperor's intent, some court ministers petitioned to restore Yinreng as crown prince, but the emperor refused. Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Lao Zhibian submitted a memorial; the emperor denounced him as treacherous and deceitful, stripped him of office, and had him beaten with the rod.
25
既，上召諸大臣，命於諸皇子中舉孰可繼立為太子者，諸大臣舉允禩。 明日，上召諸大臣入見，諭以太子因魘魅失本性狀。 諸大臣奏：「上既灼知太子病源，治療就痊，請上頒旨宣示。 」又明日，召允礽及諸大臣同入見，命釋之，且曰：「覽古史冊，太子既廢，常不得其死，人君靡不悔者。 前執允礽，朕日日不釋於懷。 自頃召見一次，胸中乃疏快一次。 今事已明白，明日為始，朕當霍然矣。 」又明日，諸大臣奏請復立允礽為太子，疏留中未下。 上疾漸愈，四十八年正月，諸大臣复疏請，上許之。
Thereafter the emperor summoned the senior ministers and ordered them to name which prince could succeed as crown prince. The ministers named Yunsi. The next day the emperor summoned the ministers and explained how the crown prince had lost his true nature through sorcery. The ministers memorialized: "Your Majesty has clearly identified the source of the crown prince's illness, and treatment has brought recovery. We beg Your Majesty to issue an edict proclaiming this." The next day he summoned Yinreng and the ministers together, ordered his release, and said: "Reading the histories, once a crown prince is deposed he seldom dies a natural death, and no ruler fails to regret it. When I earlier seized Yinreng, day after day I could not put it from my mind. Each time I have summoned him since, my heart has grown lighter. Now the matter is clear. From tomorrow onward I shall be entirely at ease." The next day the ministers again memorialized to restore Yinreng as crown prince. The memorial was retained at court and not promulgated. As the emperor gradually recovered, in the first month of the forty-eighth year the ministers memorialized again, and the emperor consented.
26
三月辛巳，復立允礽為皇太子，妃復為皇太子妃。 五十年十月，上察諸大臣為太子結黨會飲，譴責步軍統領託合齊，尚書耿額、齊世武，都統鄂繕、迓圖。 託合齊兼坐受戶部缺主沈天生賄罪，絞； 又以鎮國公景熙首告貪婪不法諸事，未決，死於獄，命剉屍焚之。 齊世武、耿額亦以得沈天生賄，絞死。 鄂繕奪官，幽禁。 迓圖入辛者庫，守安親王墓。 上諭謂：「諸事皆因允礽。 允礽不仁不孝，徒以言語貨財囑此輩貪得諂媚之人，潛通消息，尤無恥之甚。 」
On xinsi in the third month Yinreng was again installed as crown prince, and his consort again as crown princess. In the tenth month of the fiftieth year the emperor discovered that senior ministers had formed factions around the crown prince and held drinking gatherings. He rebuked Infantry Commander Tuoheqi, Ministers Geng'e and Qishiwu, and Banner Generals Echan and Yatu. Tuoheqi was also convicted of accepting bribes from Shen Tiansheng, chief clerk of a vacancy in the Ministry of Revenue, and was strangled; Duke of the State Supporting the Nation Jingxi had been the first to report his greed and unlawful conduct. Before the case was decided he died in prison, and the emperor ordered his corpse dismembered and burned. Qishiwu and Geng'e were likewise strangled for receiving bribes from Shen Tiansheng. Echan was stripped of office and confined. Yatu was sent to the Sinners' Department to guard the tomb of Prince An. The emperor said: "All these affairs stem from Yinreng. Yinreng is cruel and unfilial. He merely uses words and money to set these greedy flatterers to pass secret messages—the height of shamelessness." "
27
五十一年十月，复廢太子，禁錮咸安宮。 五十二年，趙申喬疏請立太子，上諭曰：「建儲大事，未可輕言。 允礽為太子時，服御俱用黃色，儀注上幾於朕，實開驕縱之門。 宋仁宗三十年未立太子，我太祖、太宗亦未豫立。 漢、唐已事，太子幼衝，尚保無事； 若太子年長，左右群小結黨營私，鮮有能無過者。 太子為國本，朕豈不知？ 立非其人，關係匪輕。 允礽儀表、學問、才技俱有可觀，而行事乖謬，不仁不孝，非狂易而何？ 凡人幼時猶可教訓，及長而誘於黨類，便各有所為，不復能拘制矣。 立皇太子事，未可輕定。 」自是上意不欲更立太子，雖諭大學士、九卿等裁定太子儀仗，卒未用。 終清世不復立太子。
In the tenth month of the fifty-first year the crown prince was again deposed and confined in the Xian'an Palace. In the fifty-second year Zhao Shenqiao memorialized requesting the establishment of a crown prince. The emperor said: "The great matter of establishing an heir must not be spoken of lightly. When Yinreng was crown prince his apparel and equipage were all yellow, and his ceremonial nearly equaled my own—truly opening the door to arrogance and indulgence. Song Renzong went thirty years without establishing a crown prince, and our Taizu and Taizong likewise did not establish one in advance. In Han and Tang precedents, when the crown prince was young, the realm still remained untroubled; but when the crown prince is grown, petty men at his side form factions for private gain, and few escape fault. The crown prince is the foundation of the state—do I not know this? To establish the wrong man is no small matter. Yinreng's bearing, learning, and talents are all commendable, yet his conduct is perverse, cruel, and unfilial—if not mania, what is it? While a man is young he may still be instructed; once grown and seduced by faction, each goes his own way and can no longer be restrained. The matter of establishing a crown prince must not be lightly decided." From this point the emperor did not wish to establish another crown prince. Although he ordered the grand secretaries and the Nine Ministers to fix the crown prince's ceremonial regalia, it was never used. Throughout the Qing dynasty a crown prince was never again established.
28
五十四年十一月，有醫賀孟頫者，為允礽福金治疾，允礽以礬水作書相往來，复囑普奇舉為大將軍，事發，普奇等皆得罪。 五十六年，大學士王掞疏請建儲，越數日，御史陳嘉猷等八人疏繼上，上疑其結黨，疏留中不下。 五十七年二月，翰林院檢討朱天保請復立允礽為太子，上親召詰責，辭連其父侍郎朱都納，及都統銜齊世，副都統戴保、常賚，內閣學士金寶。 朱天保、戴保誅死，朱都納及常賚、金寶交步軍統領枷示，齊世交宗人府幽禁。 七月，允礽福金石氏卒。 上稱其淑孝寬和，作配允礽，辛勤歷有年所，諭大學士等同翰林院撰文致祭。 六十年三月，上萬壽節，掞復申前請建儲。 越數日，御史陶彝等十二人疏繼上。 上乃嚴旨斥掞為奸，並以諸大臣請逮掞等治罪，上令掞及彝等發軍前委署額外章京。 掞年老，其子奕清代行。
In the eleventh month of the fifty-fourth year the physician He Mengfu treated Yinreng's primary consort. Yinreng used alum water to write secret letters back and forth and again urged Puqi to recommend him as commander-in-chief. When the plot was exposed, Puqi and the others were all punished. In the fifty-sixth year Grand Secretary Wang Yan memorialized requesting the establishment of an heir. Within several days Censor Chen Jiayou and seven others submitted memorials in succession. The emperor suspected a faction and retained the memorials without promulgating them. In the second month of the fifty-seventh year Hanlin Compiler Zhu Tianbao requested the restoration of Yinreng as crown prince. The emperor personally summoned and interrogated him. His testimony implicated his father, Vice Minister Zhu Duna, Banner General Qi Shi, Vice Banner Generals Dai Bao and Chang Ci, and Grand Secretariat Academician Jin Bao. Zhu Tianbao and Dai Bao were executed. Zhu Duna, Chang Ci, and Jin Bao were handed to the Infantry Commander for display in the cangue. Qi Shi was handed to the Imperial Clan Court for confinement. In the seventh month Yinreng's primary consort, Lady Shi, died. The emperor praised her as virtuous, filial, generous, and gentle, having been Yinreng's consort and having served diligently for many years, and ordered the grand secretaries and the Hanlin Academy to compose a memorial text for the offering. In the third month of the sixtieth year, on the emperor's birthday, Wang Yan again renewed his earlier request to establish an heir. Within several days Censor Tao Yi and eleven others submitted memorials in succession. The emperor then issued a stern edict denouncing Wang Yan as treacherous. When the senior ministers requested that Yan and the others be arrested and punished, the emperor ordered Yan, Tao Yi, and the rest dispatched to the army front as acting extra clerks. Wang Yan was elderly, and his son Yiqing went in his place.
29
六十一年，世宗即位，封允礽子弘晳為理郡王。 雍正元年，詔於祁縣鄭家莊修蓋房屋，駐劄兵丁，將移允礽往居之。 二年十二月，允礽病薨，追封諡。 六年，弘晳進封親王。 乾隆四年十月，高宗諭責弘晳，自視為東宮嫡子，居心叵測，削爵。 以允礽第十子弘㬙襲郡王。 四十五年，薨，諡曰恪。 子永曖，襲貝勒。 子孫循例遞降，以輔國公世襲。 允礽第三子弘晉、第六子弘曣、第七子弘晁、第十二子弘晥皆封輔國公。 弘曣卒，諡恪僖。 子永瑋，襲。 事高宗，歷官左宗正，廣州、黑龍江、盛京將軍。 卒，諡恪勤。 永曖四世孫福錕，事德宗，官至體仁閣大學士。 卒，諡文慎。
In the sixty-first year, when the Yongzheng Emperor acceded, he enfeoffed Yinreng's son Hongxi as Prince Li of the Second Rank. In the first year of the Yongzheng reign an edict ordered houses built at Zhengjiazhuang in Qi County with garrison troops stationed there, intending to move Yinreng there to live. In the twelfth month of the second year Yinreng died of illness, and a posthumous title was conferred. In the sixth year Hongxi was advanced to Prince of the First Rank. In the tenth month of the fourth year of the Qianlong reign the Qianlong Emperor rebuked Hongxi for regarding himself as the legitimate son of the Eastern Palace with unfathomable intent and stripped his title. Yinreng's tenth son Hongdi inherited the title of Prince of the Second Rank. In the forty-fifth year he died; his posthumous title was Ke. His son Yong'ai inherited the title of beile. Descendants followed the usual rule of successive reduction in rank, with the title of Duke of the State Assisting the Nation passing in hereditary succession. Yinreng's third son Hongjin, sixth son Hongyan, seventh son Hongchao, and twelfth son Hongwan were all enfeoffed as Duke of the State Assisting the Nation. Hongyan died; his posthumous title was Kexi. His son Yongwei inherited the title. Serving the Qianlong Emperor, he held the posts of Left Director of the Imperial Clan and Military Governor of Guangzhou, Heilongjiang, and Mukden. He died; his posthumous title was Keqin. Yong'ai's fourth-generation descendant Fukun served the Guangxu Emperor and rose to Grand Secretary of the Hall of Esteeming Benevolence. He died; his posthumous title was Wenshen.
30
誠隱郡王允祉，聖祖第三子。 康熙二十九年七月，偕皇太子詣古魯富爾堅嘉渾噶山行宮，上命先還。
Prince Chengyin of the Second Rank Yinzhi was Kangxi's third son. In the seventh month of the twenty-ninth year of the Kangxi reign he went with the crown prince to the traveling palace at Gurufurjianggahunga Mountain, and the emperor ordered them to return first.
31
三十二年，闕里孔廟成，命偕皇四子往祭。 凡行圍、謁陵，皆從。
In the thirty-second year, when the Confucian temple at Qufu was completed, he was ordered to go with the fourth prince to offer sacrifice. On hunts and visits to the imperial tombs he always accompanied the emperor.
32
三十五年，上親征，允祉領鑲紅旗大營。
In the thirty-fifth year, when the emperor led the campaign in person, Yinzhi commanded the main camp of the Bordered Red Banner.
33
三十七年三月，封誠郡王。
In the third month of the thirty-seventh year he was created Prince Cheng of the Second Rank.
34
三十八年，敏妃之喪未百日，允祉薙髮，坐降貝勒，王府長史以下譴黜有差。
In the thirty-eighth year, before a hundred days had passed since Consort Min's death, Yinzhi shaved his head. He was demoted to beile, and the prince's mansion steward and those below were rebuked and dismissed in varying degrees.
35
四十三年，命勘三門底柱。
In the forty-third year he was ordered to survey the pillars at the bottom of the Three Gates.
36
四十六年三月，迎上幸其邸園，侍宴。 嗣是，歲以為常，或一歲再幸。
In the third month of the forty-sixth year he welcomed the emperor to his mansion garden and attended the banquet. Thereafter this became an annual custom, and sometimes the emperor visited twice in a year.
37
四十七年，太子既廢，上以允祉與太子索親睦，召問太子情狀，且曰：「允祉與允礽雖暱，然未慫恿其為惡，故不罪也。 」蒙古喇嘛巴漢格隆為允禔厭勝廢太子，允祉偵得之，發其事。 明年，太子復立，允祉進封誠親王。
In the forty-seventh year, after the crown prince was deposed, the emperor summoned Yinzhi—who had been on intimate terms with the crown prince—to question him about the crown prince's conduct, and said: "Though Yinzhi was close to Yinreng, he did not urge him to do evil, and therefore is not punished." The Mongol Lama Bahangelong had used sorcery at Yunzhi's behest to bring down the crown prince. Yinzhi detected it and exposed the affair. The following year, when the crown prince was restored, Yinzhi was advanced to Prince Cheng of the First Rank.
38
五十一年，賜銀五千。
In the fifty-first year five thousand taels of silver were bestowed on him.
39
聖祖邃律曆之學，命允祉率庶吉士何國宗等輯律呂、算法諸書，諭曰：「古歷規模甚好，但其數目歲久不合。 今修曆書，規模宜存古，數目宜準今。 」
Kangxi was deeply versed in pitch-pipes and calendrical learning and ordered Yinzhi to lead Hanlin bachelors He Guozong and others in compiling books on pitch-pipes and calculation, instructing: "The ancient calendar's framework is excellent, but its figures no longer accord after long years. In revising the calendar now, the framework should preserve the ancient, but the figures should accord with the present." "
40
五十三年十一月，書成，奏進。 上命以律呂、曆法、算法三者合為一書，名曰《律曆淵源》。
In the eleventh month of the fifty-third year the book was completed and presented to the throne. The emperor ordered the three—pitch-pipes, calendrical method, and calculation—combined into one book titled 《Origins of Pitch-Pipes and Calendrical Learning》.
41
五十八年，上有事於圜丘，拜畢，命允祉行禮。
In the fifty-eighth year, when the emperor performed rites at the Circular Mound Altar, after the bowing was completed he ordered Yinzhi to perform the rites.
42
五十九年，封子弘晟為世子，班俸視貝子。
In the fifty-ninth year his son Hongcheng was enfeoffed as heir apparent, with stipend and precedence equal to a beizi.
43
六十年，上命弘晟偕皇四子、皇十二子祭盛京三陵。 世宗即位，命允祉守護景陵。
In the sixtieth year the emperor ordered Hongcheng, together with the fourth prince and the twelfth prince, to sacrifice at the three tombs of Mukden. When the Yongzheng Emperor acceded he ordered Yinzhi to guard the Jing Mausoleum.
44
雍正二年，弘晟得罪，削世子，為閑散宗室。
In the second year of the Yongzheng reign Hongcheng offended and was stripped of heir-apparent status, becoming an unattached member of the imperial clan.
45
六年六月，允祉索蘇克濟賕，事發，在上前詰王大臣，上責其無臣禮，議奪爵，錮私第。 上曰：「朕止此一兄。 朕兄弟如允祉者何限？ 皆欲激朕治其罪，其心誠不可喻。 良亦朕不能感化所致，未可謂盡若輩之罪也。 」命降郡王，而歸其罪於弘晟，交宗人府禁錮。
In the sixth month of the sixth year Yinzhi demanded a bribe from Sukeji. When the affair came to light he interrogated the princes and ministers before the emperor, who rebuked him for lacking the deportment of a subject. It was deliberated to strip his title and confine him in his private residence. The emperor said: "I have only this one elder brother. How many brothers like Yinzhi do I have? All wish to provoke me into punishing him—their intent truly cannot be fathomed. It is also because I could not reform him by influence; one cannot say the fault lies entirely with such men." He was reduced to Prince of the Second Rank, the guilt attributed to Hongcheng, who was handed to the Imperial Clan Court for confinement.
46
八年二月，復進封親王。 五月，怡親王之喪，允祉後至，無戚容。 莊親王允祿等劾，下宗人府議，奏稱：「允祉乖張不孝，暱近陳夢雷、周昌言，祈禳鎮魘，與阿其那、塞思黑、允禵交相黨附。 其子弘晟凶頑狂縱，助父為惡，僅予禁錮，而允祉銜恨怨懟。 怡親王忠孝性成，允祉心懷嫉忌，並不懇請持服，王府齊集，遲至早散，背理蔑倫，當削爵。 」與其子弘晟皆論死。 上命奪爵，禁景山永安亭，聽家屬與偕，弘晟仍禁宗人府。
In the second month of the eighth year he was again advanced to Prince of the First Rank. In the fifth month, at Prince Yi's mourning, Yinzhi arrived late and showed no sign of grief. Prince Zhuang Yunlu and others impeached him. The case was referred to the Imperial Clan Court, which memorialized: "Yinzhi is perverse and unfilial, intimate with Chen Menglei and Zhou Changyan, employs prayer and sorcery, and forms a faction with Aqina, Seshei, and Yinti. His son Hongcheng is vicious, stubborn, and wildly unrestrained, aiding his father in evil. He was only placed in confinement, yet Yinzhi harbors resentment and rancor. Prince Yi was loyal and filial by nature. Yinzhi harbored jealousy, did not earnestly request to observe mourning, came late when the princes assembled at the mansion and left early—against reason and scorning propriety—and his title should be stripped." Both he and his son Hongcheng were sentenced to death. The emperor ordered his title stripped and confined him at Yong'an Pavilion on Jingshan, with family members allowed to accompany him. Hongcheng remained confined in the Imperial Clan Court.
47
十年閏五月，薨，視郡王例殯葬。 乾隆二年，追諡。 子弘暻，封貝子。 子孫遞降，以不入八分輔國公世襲。 五世孫載齡，襲爵。 事德宗，官至體仁閣大學士。 卒，諡文恪。
In the intercalary fifth month of the tenth year he died and was buried with the rites due a prince of the second rank. In the second year of the Qianlong reign a posthumous title was conferred. His son Hongjing was enfeoffed as beizi. Descendants followed successive reduction in rank, with the title of Duke of the State Assisting the Nation outside the eight privileges passing in hereditary succession. His fifth-generation descendant Zailing inherited the title. Serving the Guangxu Emperor, he rose to Grand Secretary of the Hall of Esteeming Benevolence. He died; his posthumous title was Wenke.
48
恒溫親王允祺，聖祖第五子。 康熙三十五年，上征噶爾丹，命允祺領正黃旗大營。
Prince Hengwen Yunqi was Kangxi's fifth son. In the thirty-fifth year of the Kangxi reign, when the emperor campaigned against Galdan, he ordered Yunqi to command the main camp of the Plain Yellow Banner.
49
四十八年十月，封恒親王。
In the tenth month of the forty-eighth year he was enfeoffed as Prince Heng.
50
五十一年，賜銀五千。
In the fifty-first year he was granted five thousand taels of silver.
51
五十八年，封子弘昇為世子，班祿視貝子。
In the fifty-eighth year his son Hongsheng was enfeoffed as heir apparent, with stipend and precedence equal to a beizi.
52
雍正五年，坐事，削世子。
In the fifth year of the Yongzheng reign, convicted of an offense, he was stripped of heir-apparent status.
53
十年閏五月，允祺薨，予諡。 子弘晊，襲。
In the intercalary fifth month of the tenth year Yunqi died and was granted a posthumous title. His son Hongzhi inherited the title.
54
乾隆四十年，薨，諡曰恪。 子永皓，襲郡王。
In the fortieth year of the Qianlong reign he died; his posthumous title was Ke. His son Yonghao inherited as Prince of the Second Rank.
55
五十三年，薨，諡曰敬。 弘升子永澤，襲貝子。 子孫循例遞降，以鎮國公世襲。 弘昇既削世子，乾隆十九年卒，予貝勒品級，諡恭恪。
In the fifty-third year he died; his posthumous title was Jing. Hongsheng's son Yongze inherited as beizi. Descendants followed the usual rule of successive reduction in rank, with the title of Duke of the State Supporting the Nation passing in hereditary succession. Hongsheng, who had already been stripped of heir-apparent status, died in the nineteenth year of the Qianlong reign. He was granted beile rank, and his posthumous title was Gongke.
56
淳度親王允祐，聖祖第七子。 康熙三十五年，上征噶爾丹，命允祐領鑲黃旗大營。
Prince Chundu was Kangxi's seventh son. In the thirty-fifth year of the Kangxi reign, when the emperor campaigned against Galdan, he ordered Chundu to command the main camp of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
57
三十七年三月，封貝勒。
In the third month of the thirty-seventh year he was enfeoffed as beile.
58
四十八年十月，封淳郡王。
In the tenth month of the forty-eighth year he was enfeoffed as Prince Chun of the Second Rank.
59
五十一年，賜銀五千。
In the fifty-first year he was granted five thousand taels of silver.
60
五十七年十月，正藍旗滿洲都統延信征西陲，命允祐管正藍三旗事務。
In the tenth month of the fifty-seventh year, when Yanxin, Manchu Lieutenant-General of the Plain Blue Banner, campaigned on the western frontier, Chundu was ordered to administer the affairs of the three Plain Blue Banners.
61
雍正元年，進封親王，詔褒其安分守己，敬順小心。 復命與誠親王允祉並書景陵碑額，以兩王皆工書故。
In the first year of the Yongzheng reign he was advanced to Prince of the First Rank. An edict praised him for keeping to his place and conducting himself with respectful caution. He was again ordered, together with Prince Cheng Yinzhi, to inscribe the stele at the Jing Mausoleum, because both princes were skilled in calligraphy.
62
八年四月，薨，予諡。 子弘曙。 聖祖命皇十四子允禵為撫遠大將軍，駐甘州，令弘曙從。 聖祖崩，世宗召還京，封世子。 雍正五年，坐事削，改封弘暻為世子。 允祐薨，弘暻襲。 乾隆四十二年，薨，諡曰慎。 子永鋆，襲貝勒。 子孫遞降，以鎮國公世襲。 永鋆子綿洵，事穆宗，官涼州副都統。 轉戰河南、直隸、山東、湖北，克臨清，破連鎮、馮官屯，皆有功。 遷荊州將軍。 卒，諡莊武。
In the fourth month of the eighth year he died and was granted a posthumous title. His son was Hongshu. Kangxi appointed the fourteenth prince Yinti as Grand General for the Pacification of the Distance, stationed at Ganzhou, and ordered Hongshu to accompany him. When Kangxi died the Yongzheng Emperor summoned him back to the capital and enfeoffed him as heir apparent. In the fifth year of the Yongzheng reign, convicted of an offense and stripped of the title, Hongjing was instead enfeoffed as heir apparent. When Chundu died Hongjing inherited the title. In the forty-second year of the Qianlong reign he died; his posthumous title was Shen. His son Yongjun inherited as beile. Descendants followed successive reduction in rank, with the title of Duke of the State Supporting the Nation passing in hereditary succession. Yongjun's son Mianxun served the Tongzhi Emperor and held the post of Vice Lieutenant-General of Liangzhou. Campaigning in Henan, Zhili, Shandong, and Hubei, he captured Linqing and broke the defenses at Lianzhen and Fengguantun, distinguishing himself in each action. He was transferred to Military Governor of Jingzhou. He died; his posthumous title was Zhuangwu.
63
允禩，聖祖第八子。 康熙三十七年三月，封貝勒。
Yunsi was Kangxi's eighth son. In the third month of the thirty-seventh year of the Kangxi reign he was enfeoffed as beile.
64
四十七年九月，署內務府總管事。
In the ninth month of the forty-seventh year he was appointed acting superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.
65
太子允礽既廢，允禩謀代立。 諸皇子允禟、允䄉、允禵，諸大臣阿靈阿、鄂倫岱、揆敘、王鴻緒等，皆附允禩。 允禔言於上，謂相士張明德言允禩後必大貴，上大怒，會內務府總管凌普以附太子得罪，籍其家，允禩頗庇之，上以責允禩。 諭曰：「凌普貪婪巨富，所籍未盡，允禩每妄博虛名，凡朕所施恩澤，俱歸功於己，是又一太子矣！ 如有人譽允禩，必殺無赦。 」翌日，召諸皇子入，諭曰：「當廢允礽時，朕即諭諸皇子有鑽營為皇太子者，即國之賊，法所不容。 允禩柔姦性成，妄蓄大志，黨羽相結，謀害允礽。 今其事皆敗露，即鎖系，交議政處審理。 」允禟語允禵，入為允禩營救，上怒，出佩刀將誅允禵； 允祺跪抱勸止，上怒少解，仍諭諸皇子、議政大臣等毋寬允禩罪。
After Crown Prince Yinreng had been deposed, Yunsi plotted to take his place. The princes Yuntang, Yun'e, and Yinti, and the ministers Aling'a, Olonday, Kuixu, and Wang Hongxu, all supported Yunsi. Yunzhi reported to the emperor that the physiognomist Zhang Mingde had declared Yunsi destined for great eminence. The emperor was furious. At the same time Superintendent of the Imperial Household Department Ling Pu was convicted of siding with the crown prince and his property was confiscated. Yunsi had sheltered him at length, and the emperor rebuked Yunsi. An edict declared: "Ling Pu was greedily and enormously wealthy, and what was confiscated did not exhaust his holdings. Yunsi constantly seeks empty reputation; every grace I bestow he claims for himself—he is another crown prince! If anyone praises Yunsi, he shall be put to death without pardon. " The next day the emperor summoned the princes and declared: "When Yinreng was deposed I at once told all the princes that whoever schemed to become crown prince was a traitor to the state and would not be spared by law. Yunsi is soft and treacherous by nature, harbors wild ambition, forms factions, and plots against Yinreng. Now his affairs are all exposed. He is immediately placed in fetters and handed to the Deliberative Council for trial. " Yuntang spoke to Yinti and entered the palace to plead for Yunsi. The emperor was enraged, drew his girdle knife, and was about to execute Yinti; Yunqi knelt and embraced him to restrain him. The emperor's anger eased somewhat, but he still instructed the princes and Deliberative Ministers not to leniently treat Yunsi's crime.
66
逮相士張明德會鞫，詞連順承郡王布穆巴，公賴士、普奇，順承郡王長史阿祿。 張明德坐凌遲處死，普奇奪公爵，允禩亦奪貝勒，為閑散宗室。 上復諭諸皇子曰：「允禩庇其乳母夫雅齊布，雅齊布之叔厩長吳達理與御史雍泰同榷關稅，不相能，訴之允禩，允禩借事痛責雍泰。 朕聞之，以雅齊布發翁牛特公主處。 允禩因怨朕，與褚英孫蘇努相結，敗壞國事。 允禩又受制於妻，妻為安郡王岳樂甥，嫉妒行惡，是以允禩尚未生子。 此皆爾曹所知，爾曹當遵朕旨，方是為臣子之理； 若不如此存心，日後朕考終，必至將朕躬置乾清宮內，束甲相爭耳。 」上幸南苑，遘疾，還宮，召允禩入見，並召太子使居咸安宮。
When the physiognomist Zhang Mingde was jointly tried, his testimony implicated Prince Shuncheng of the Second Rank Bumuba, Gonglaishi, Puqi, and Prince Shuncheng's chief secretary Alu. Zhang Mingde was sentenced to death by lingchi. Puqi was stripped of his ducal rank. Yunsi was also stripped of beile rank and became an unattached member of the imperial clan. The emperor again instructed the princes: "Yunsi sheltered his wet nurse's husband Yaqibu. Yaqibu's uncle, stable chief Wudali, and Censor Yongtai jointly collected transit duties and could not get along. Wudali appealed to Yunsi, and Yunsi seized the occasion to harshly rebuke Yongtai. When I learned of it I sent Yaqibu to the territory of the Ongniot princess. Yunsi therefore resented me, joined with Sunu, grandson of Nurhaci's eldest son Cuying, and corrupted state affairs. Yunsi is also controlled by his wife. His wife is a niece of Prince An of the Second Rank Yuele, jealous and wicked in conduct, and therefore Yunsi has not yet had a son. All this you know. You should follow my instructions—only then is the principle of subject and minister fulfilled; if you do not keep such intent in mind, after my death you will surely put my person in the Palace of Heavenly Purity and fight one another in armor. " The emperor went to the Southern Park, fell ill, and returned to the palace. He summoned Yunsi for an audience and also had the crown prince dwell in the Xian'an Palace.
67
未幾，上命諸大臣於諸皇子中舉可為太子者，阿靈阿等私示意諸大臣舉允禩。 上曰：「允禩未更事，且罹罪，其母亦微賤，宜別舉。 」上釋允礽，亦復允禩貝勒。 四十八年正月，上召諸大臣，問倡舉允禩為太子者，諸臣不敢質言。 上以大學士馬齊先言眾欲舉允禩，因譴馬齊，不復深詰。 尋復立允礽為太子。 五十一年十一月，复廢允礽。
Before long the emperor ordered the senior ministers to name among the princes who could become crown prince. Aling'a and others privately signaled the ministers to name Yunsi. The emperor said: "Yunsi lacks experience in affairs, has moreover been convicted, and his mother is also of low birth. Another should be chosen. " The emperor released Yinreng and also restored Yunsi as beile. In the first month of the forty-eighth year the emperor summoned the senior ministers and asked who had advocated naming Yunsi as crown prince. The ministers did not dare speak plainly. Because Grand Secretary Ma Qi had first said the multitude wished to name Yunsi, the emperor rebuked Ma Qi and did not pursue the matter further. Soon afterward Yinreng was again installed as crown prince. In the eleventh month of the fifty-first year Yinreng was again deposed.
68
六十一年十一月，上疾大漸，召允禩及諸皇子允祉、允祐、允禟、允䄉、允祹、允祥同受末命。 世宗即位，命允禩總理事務，進封廉親王，授理籓院尚書。 雍正元年，命辦理工部事務。 皇太子允礽之廢也，允禩謀繼立，世宗深憾之。 允禩亦知世宗憾之深也，居常怏怏。 封親王命下，其福晉烏雅氏對賀者曰：「何賀為？ 慮不免首領耳！ 」語聞，世宗憾滋甚。 會副都統祁爾薩條奏：「滿洲俗遇喪，親友饋粥吊慰。 後風俗漸弛，大設奢饌，過事奢靡。 」上用其議申禁，因諭斥：「允禩居母妃喪，沽孝名，百日後猶扶掖匍匐而行； 而允䄉，允禟、允指稱饋食，大肆筵席，皇考諭責者屢矣。 」二年，上諭曰：「允禩素行陰狡，皇考所深知，降旨不可悉數。 自朕即位，優封親王，任以總理事務。 乃不能輸其誠悃以輔朕躬，懷挾私心，至今未已。 凡事欲激朕怒以治其罪，加朕以不令之名。 允禩在諸弟中頗有治事材，朕甚愛惜之，非允禟、允䄉等可比，是以屢加教誨，令其改過，不但成朕友於之誼，亦全前三復教誨之理？ 朕一身上關宗廟社稷，不得不為？ 皇考慈愛之衷。 朕果欲治其罪，豈有於防範。 允禩在皇考時，恣意妄行，匪伊朝夕，朕可不念祖宗肇造鴻圖，以永貽子孫之安乎？ 」
In the eleventh month of the sixty-first year, as the emperor's illness grew critical, he summoned Yunsi and the princes Yinzhi, Chundu, Yuntang, Yun'e, Yunyou, and Yinxiang together to receive his final command. When the Yongzheng Emperor acceded he ordered Yunsi to oversee general affairs, advanced him to Prince Lian, and appointed him Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs. In the first year of the Yongzheng reign he was ordered to manage the affairs of the Ministry of Works. When Crown Prince Yinreng was deposed, Yunsi had plotted to succeed him. The Yongzheng Emperor deeply resented this. Yunsi also knew how deeply the Yongzheng Emperor resented him and was habitually discontented. When the order enfeoffing him as prince of the first rank was issued, his primary consort of the Uya clan said to those offering congratulations: "What is there to congratulate? I fear we cannot keep our heads! " When word reached the Yongzheng Emperor his resentment grew still deeper. It happened that Vice Lieutenant-General Qierisa memorialized: "In Manchu custom, when there is mourning friends and relatives bring congee in condolence. Later the custom gradually lapsed. Lavish feasts were spread and extravagance was carried too far. " The emperor adopted his proposal and issued a prohibition, then denounced: "When Yunsi was in mourning for his imperial consort mother he traded on the name of filial piety. Even after the hundred days he still walked supported and crawling on the ground; whereas Yun'e, Yuntang, and Yinti, under the pretext of bringing food in condolence, spread great banquets—the late emperor had rebuked them many times. " In the second year the emperor declared: "Yunsi has always been secretly treacherous. The late emperor knew this thoroughly, and the edicts denouncing him cannot all be counted. Since I acceded I have graciously enfeoffed him as prince and entrusted him with overseeing general affairs. Yet he cannot offer his sincere loyalty to assist me and still harbors private intent. In every matter he wishes to provoke my anger so that I may punish him and give me an ill name. Among my younger brothers Yunsi has considerable talent for governing affairs. I greatly cherish him, and he is not to be compared with Yuntang, Yun'e, and the like. Therefore I have repeatedly admonished him and ordered him to reform—not only to fulfill the bond of brotherhood between us, but also to complete the principle of thrice repeated admonition? My person alone bears upon the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain—I cannot but act? I must act for the late emperor's loving intent. If I truly wished to punish him, would there be any need for precaution? Under the late emperor Yunsi acted willfully and recklessly—not for a day or two. Can I fail to remember how our ancestors founded this great enterprise, so as to secure peace for posterity? "
69
三年二月，三年服滿。 以允禩任總理事務，挾私懷詐，有罪無功，不予議敘。 尋因工部製祈榖壇祖宗神牌草率，阿爾泰駐兵軍器粗窳，屢下詔詰責允禩； 允禩議減內務府披甲，上令覆奏，又請一佐領增甲九十餘副。 上以允禩前後異議，諭謂：「陰邪叵測，莫此為甚！ 」因命一佐領留甲五十副不即裁，待缺出不補。 隸內務府披甲諸人集允禩邸囂閧，翌日，又集副都統李延禧家，且縱掠。 上命捕治，諸人自列允禩使閧延禧家，允禩不置辯。 上命允禩鞫定為首者立斬，允禩以五人姓名上，上察其一乃自首，其一堅稱病未往，責允禩所讞不實。 宗人府議奪允禩爵，上命寬之。 允禩杖殺護軍九十六，命太監閻倫隱其事，厚賜之。 宗人府复議奪允禩爵，上复寬之。
In the second month of the third year the three-year mourning period was completed. Because Yunsi, while overseeing general affairs, harbored private intent and deceit and had guilt but no merit, he was not granted deliberative honors. Soon afterward, because the ancestral tablets for the Prayer for Grain Altar made by the Ministry of Works were careless and the garrison arms under Altai's command were crude, edicts repeatedly rebuked Yunsi; Yunsi proposed reducing the armor of the Imperial Household Department. The emperor ordered a memorial in reply, and he then requested adding more than ninety sets of armor to one company. Because Yunsi's proposals before and after differed, an edict declared: "Secretly treacherous and unfathomable—nothing surpasses this! " He therefore ordered one company to retain fifty sets of armor and not cut them immediately; when vacancies occurred they would not be filled. Those subordinate to the Imperial Household Department who wore armor gathered at Yunsi's mansion in uproar. The next day they gathered again at Vice Lieutenant-General Li Yanxi's house and even plundered freely. The emperor ordered them seized and punished. The men themselves reported that Yunsi had incited the uproar at Yanxi's house, and Yunsi offered no defense. The emperor ordered Yunsi to try the ringleaders and execute them on the spot. Yunsi submitted five names, but the emperor found that one man had surrendered himself and another insisted he had been too ill to go. He rebuked Yunsi for presenting a false case. The Imperial Clan Court recommended stripping Yunsi of his title, but the emperor ordered leniency. Yunsi had ninety-six guardsmen beaten to death, then ordered the eunuch Yan Lun to cover it up and rewarded him handsomely. The Imperial Clan Court again recommended stripping Yunsi of his title, and again the emperor showed leniency.
70
四年正月，上御西暖閣，召諸王大臣暴允禩罪狀，略曰：「當時允禩希冀非望，欲沽忠孝之名，而事事傷聖祖之心。 二阿哥坐廢，聖祖命朕與允禩在京辦事，凡有啟奏，皆蒙御批，由允禩藏貯。 嗣問允禩，則曰：'前值皇考怒，恐不測，故焚毀筆札，禦批亦納其中。 '此允禩親向朕言者。 聖祖升遐，朕念允禩夙有才幹，冀其痛改其非，為國家出力，令其總理事務，加封親王，推心置腹。 三年以來，宗人府及諸大臣劾議，什伯累積，朕百端容忍，乃允禩詭譎陰邪，狂妄悖亂，包藏禍心，日益加甚。 朕令宗人府訊問何得將皇考禦批焚毀，允禩改言：'抱病昏昧，誤行燒毀。 '及朕面質之，公然設誓，詛及一家。 允禩自絕於天，自絕於祖宗，自絕於朕，斷不可留於宗姓之內，為我朝之玷！ 謹述皇考諭，遵先朝削籍離宗之典，革去允禩黃帶子，以儆兇邪，為萬世子孫鑑戒。 」並命逐其福晉還外家。
In the first month of the fourth year, the Yongzheng Emperor held court in the West Warm Pavilion and summoned the princes and senior ministers to proclaim Yunsi's crimes. He said in summary: "At that time Yunsi harbored improper ambitions and sought a reputation for loyalty and filial piety, yet in everything he did he wounded Kangxi's heart. When the second prince was deposed, Kangxi ordered me and Yunsi to manage affairs in the capital. Every memorial submitted received the emperor's vermilion rescript, and Yunsi was charged with keeping them. When Yunsi was later questioned, he said: 'When my late father was angry, I feared what might happen, so I burned the letters and papers—and the imperial rescripts were among them. ' This is what Yunsi personally told me. After Kangxi's death, I remembered Yunsi's long-standing talent and hoped he would thoroughly reform and serve the state. I put him in charge of general affairs, enfeoffed him as a prince of the first rank, and treated him with complete trust. Over three years the Imperial Clan Court and senior ministers piled up impeachments by the dozens, and I tolerated them in every way I could. Yet Yunsi grew ever more deceitful and treacherous, wildly rebellious and full of hidden malice. I ordered the Imperial Clan Court to ask how he could have burned my late father's imperial rescripts. Yunsi changed his story: 'I was ill and confused and burned them by mistake. ' When I confronted him directly, he openly swore an oath that cursed the entire imperial house. Yunsi has cut himself off from Heaven, from the ancestors, and from me. He cannot remain within the imperial clan and become a stain on our dynasty! In keeping with my late father's instruction and the precedent of expulsion from the clan register, I strip Yunsi of the yellow girdle to warn the vicious and treacherous and provide a lesson for all future generations. " He also ordered Yunsi's primary consort expelled and sent back to her natal family.
71
二月，授允禩為民王，不留所屬佐領人員，凡朝會，視民公、侯、伯例，稱親王允禩。 諸王大臣請誅允禩，上不許。 尋命削王爵，交宗人府圈禁高牆。 宗人府請更名編入佐領：​​允禩改名阿其那，子弘旺改菩薩保。 六月，諸王大臣复臚允禩罪狀四十事，請與允禟、允並正典刑，上暴其罪於中外。 九月，允禩患嘔噦，命給與調養，未幾卒於幽所。 諸王大臣仍請戮屍，不許。
In the second month Yunsi was reduced to a commoner prince. His company personnel were removed, and at court assemblies he was treated like a commoner duke, marquis, or earl while still being addressed as Prince Yunsi. The princes and senior ministers asked that Yunsi be executed, but the emperor refused. Soon afterward he was stripped of princely rank and handed over to the Imperial Clan Court for confinement within the high walls. The Imperial Clan Court requested that he be renamed and enrolled in a company: Yunsi was renamed Aqina, and his son Hongwang was renamed Pusa Bao. In the sixth month the princes and senior ministers again listed forty counts against Yunsi and asked that he, together with Yuntang and Yinti, be punished according to law. The emperor made their crimes known throughout the realm. In the ninth month Yunsi suffered vomiting and hiccups. Medical care was ordered for him, but before long he died in confinement. The princes and senior ministers again asked that his corpse be mutilated, but the request was denied.
72
乾隆四十三年正月，高宗諭曰：「聖祖第八子允禩，第九子允禟結黨妄行，罪皆自取。 皇考僅令削籍更名，以示愧辱。 就兩人心術而論，覬覦窺竊，誠所不免，及皇考紹登大寶。 皇考晚年屢向朕諭及，愀然不樂，意頗悔？ ，怨尤誹謗，亦情事所有，特未有顯然悖逆之之，若將有待。 朕今臨御四十三年矣，此事重大，朕若不言，後世子孫無敢言者。 允禩、允禟仍復原名，收入玉牒，子孫一併？ 入。 此實仰體皇考仁心，申未竟之緒，想在天之靈​​亦當愉慰也。 」
In the first month of the forty-third year of the Qianlong reign, the Qianlong Emperor issued an edict: "Kangxi's eighth son Yunsi and ninth son Yuntang formed factions and acted recklessly. Their crimes were entirely of their own making. My late father only ordered them expelled from the clan register and renamed, to mark their shame and disgrace. Judging the two men's character, covetous ambition and secret scheming were indeed hard to avoid. Yet once my late father succeeded to the throne, in his later years my late father often spoke to me of the matter, grave and unhappy, and was quite regretful? Resentment and slander were also to be expected, yet there had been no clearly rebellious acts, as if he were waiting to see what might happen. I have now reigned for forty-three years. This matter is too important: if I do not speak, no descendant in later ages will dare to do so. Yunsi and Yuntang shall have their original names restored and be entered in the imperial genealogy, and their descendants shall also all be? entered in the genealogy as well. This truly honors my late father's benevolent intent and completes what he left unfinished. Surely his spirit in Heaven will also be pleased and comforted. "
73
允禟，聖祖第九子。 康熙四十七年，上責允禩，允禟語允，入為保奏，上怒。 是時，上每巡幸，輒隨。 四十八年三月，封貝子。 十月，命往翁牛特送和碩慍恪公主之喪。 五十一年，賜銀四千。
Yuntang was Kangxi's ninth son. In the forty-seventh year of the Kangxi reign the emperor rebuked Yunsi. Yuntang spoke to Yinti and entered the palace to intercede on his behalf, and the emperor was enraged. At that time he always accompanied the emperor whenever Kangxi went on tour. In the third month of the forty-eighth year he was enfeoffed as beizi. In the tenth month he was ordered to go to Ongniut to escort the funeral of Princess Wenke of the first rank. In the fifty-first year he was granted four thousand taels of silver.
74
雍正元年，世宗召允回京，以諸王大臣議，命允禟出駐西寧。 允禟屢請緩行，上譴責所屬太監，允禟行至軍。 二年四月，宗人府劾允禟擅遣人至河州買草、勘牧地，違法肆行，請奪爵，上命寬之。 三年，上聞允禟縱容家下人在西寧生事，遣都統楚宗往約束，楚宗至，允禟不出迎，傳旨詰責，曰：「上責我皆是，我復何言？ 我行將出家離世！ 」楚宗以聞，上以允禟傲慢無人臣禮，手詔深責之，並牽連及允禩、允、允䄉私結黨援諸事。 七月，山烏雅圖等經平定毆諸生，請按律治罪，陝西人稱允禟九王，為上？ 西巡撫伊都立奏劾允禟護所聞，手詔斥為無恥，遂奪允禟爵，撤所屬佐領，即西寧幽禁，並錄允禟左右用事者毛太、佟保等，撤還京師，授以官。
In the first year of the Yongzheng reign the Yongzheng Emperor recalled Yinti to the capital. On the deliberation of the princes and senior ministers, Yuntang was ordered to take up station at Xining. Yuntang repeatedly asked to delay his departure. The emperor rebuked the eunuchs under him, and Yuntang eventually reached Xining. In the fourth month of the second year the Imperial Clan Court impeached Yuntang for sending men on his own authority to Hezhou to buy fodder and survey pasture lands in violation of the law and recommended stripping his title. The emperor ordered leniency. In the third year the emperor heard that Yuntang was allowing his household servants to make trouble at Xining and dispatched Lieutenant-General Chuzong to restrain them. When Chuzong arrived, Yuntang did not come out to receive him. The transmitted edict rebuked him, saying: "The emperor's rebukes of me are all justified—what more can I say? I am about to leave home and quit the world! " Chuzong reported this. Because Yuntang was arrogant and showed none of a subject's propriety, the emperor personally drafted an edict sharply rebuking him and also raised Yunsi's, Yinti's, and Yun'e's private factional ties. In the seventh month Shan Wuyatu and others beat local students while passing through Pingding and asked that they be punished according to law. People in Shaanxi called Yuntang the Ninth Prince, and this reached the emperor? The Shaanxi governor Yiduli memorialized impeaching Yuntang for shielding those involved. A personally drafted edict denounced this as shameless. Yuntang's title was stripped, his companies withdrawn, and he was immediately confined at Xining. Mao Tai, Tong Bao, and others who wielded power at Yuntang's side were enrolled, recalled to the capital, and given official posts.
75
四年正月，九門捕役得毛太、佟保等寄允禟私書，以聞，上見書跡類西洋字，遣持問允禟子弘暘，弘暘言允禟所造字也。 諭曰：「從來造作隱語，防人察覺，惟敵國為然。 允禟在西寧，未嘗禁其書札往來，何至別造字體，暗藏密遞，不可令人以共見耶？ 允禟與弘暘書用朱筆，弘暘復書稱其父言為'旨'，皆僭妄非禮。 允禟寄允䄉書言'事機已失'，其言尤駭人。 」命嚴鞫毛太、佟保等。 諸王大臣請治允禟罪，命革去黃帶子，削宗籍，逮還京，令胡什禮監以行。 五月，令允禟改名，又以所擬字樣姦巧，下諸王大臣議，改為塞？ 楚宗及侍思黑。
In the first month of the fourth year the Nine Gates constables seized private letters from Mao Tai and Tong Bao to Yuntang and reported them. The emperor saw that the script resembled Western letters and sent men to question Yuntang's son Hongyang, who said they were characters Yuntang had invented. An edict said: "From antiquity only enemy states have invented secret language to keep others from detecting their meaning. Yuntang at Xining was never forbidden to exchange letters—so why invent a separate script and pass secret messages that could not be shown openly? Letters between Yuntang and Hongyang were written in vermilion ink, and in his replies Hongyang called his father's words an 'edict'—all presumptuous and improper. In a letter to Yun'e, Yuntang wrote that 'the opportunity is already lost'—words especially shocking to read. " He ordered Mao Tai, Tong Bao, and the others to be strictly interrogated. The princes and senior ministers asked that Yuntang be punished. He was stripped of the yellow girdle, expunged from the clan register, seized and brought back to the capital under the escort of Hushili. In the fifth month Yuntang was ordered to change his name. Because the characters he proposed were too crafty, the matter was submitted to the princes and senior ministers for deliberation, and the name was changed to Se? —completing the new name Seshei.
76
六月，諸王大臣复劾允禟罪狀二十八事，請誅之。 胡什禮監允禟至保定，命直隸總督李紱暫禁，觀其行止。 紱語胡什禮「當便宜行事」，胡什禮以聞，上命馳諭止之，紱奏無此語。 八月，紱奏允禟以腹疾卒於幽所。 上聞胡什禮與楚宗中途械系允禟，旋釋去，胡什禮又，乃起流言也。 乾？ 妄述紱語，命並逮治。 其後紱得罪，上猶責紱不以允禟死狀明白於隆間，復原名，還宗籍。 子弘晸，封不入八分輔國公，坐事奪爵。
In the sixth month the princes and senior ministers again impeached Yuntang on twenty-eight counts and asked that he be executed. Hushili escorted Yuntang to Baoding. The Zhili governor Li Fu was ordered to hold him temporarily and observe his conduct. Li Fu told Hushili to "act as circumstances require." Hushili reported this, and the emperor ordered an urgent message to stop it. Li Fu memorialized that he had said no such thing. In the eighth month Li Fu memorialized that Yuntang had died of abdominal illness in confinement. The emperor learned that Hushili and Chuzong had shackled Yuntang midway on the journey and then released him. Hushili again acted improperly, and rumors spread. Chuzong? He falsely reported Li Fu's words, and the emperor ordered both men seized and punished. Thereafter Li Fu fell into disgrace, yet the emperor still rebuked him for not making Yuntang's cause of death clear in open court. Yuntang's original name was restored and he was returned to the clan register. His son Hongjing was enfeoffed as a fuguo gong outside the eight privileges, but later lost his title for an offense.
77
輔國公允䄉，聖祖第十子。 康熙四十八年十月，封敦郡王。 五十七年，命辦理正黃旗滿洲、蒙古、漢軍三旗事。 允䄉與允禟、允皆黨附允禩，為世宗所惡。 雍正元年，澤卜尊丹巴胡土克圖詣京師，謁聖祖梓宮，俄病卒，上遣送靈龕還喀爾喀，命允䄉齎印冊賜奠。 允䄉託疾不行，旋稱有旨召還，居張家口。 复私行禳禱，疏文內連書「雍正新君」，為上所知，斥為不敬。 兵部劾奏，命允禩議其罪。 四月，奪爵，逮京師拘禁。 乾隆二年，高宗命釋之，封輔國公。 六年，卒，詔用貝子品級祭葬。
Fuguo Gong Yun'e was Kangxi's tenth son. In the tenth month of the forty-eighth year of the Kangxi reign he was enfeoffed as Prince Dun of the second rank. In the fifty-seventh year he was ordered to manage the affairs of the Plain Yellow Banner's Manchu, Mongol, and Chinese companies. Yun'e, together with Yuntang and Yinti, all joined Yunsi's faction and were hated by the Yongzheng Emperor. In the first year of the Yongzheng reign the Jebtsundamba Khutuktu came to the capital to pay respects at Kangxi's coffin palace, but soon fell ill and died. The emperor sent the spirit casket back to Khalkha and ordered Yun'e to carry the seal and patent to grant funeral offerings. Yun'e pleaded illness and did not go. Soon he claimed there was an edict recalling him and remained at Zhangjiakou. He again privately performed prayer and exorcism rites, and in the memorial text repeatedly wrote "the new ruler Yongzheng." When the emperor learned of this he denounced it as disrespectful. The Ministry of War impeached him, and Yunsi was ordered to deliberate his crime. In the fourth month his title was stripped and he was seized and confined in the capital. In the second year of the Qianlong reign the Qianlong Emperor ordered him released and enfeoffed as fuguo gong. In the sixth year he died, and an edict ordered funeral rites at beizi rank.
78
履懿親王允祹，聖祖第十二子。 康熙四十八年十月，封貝子。 自是有巡幸，輒從。 五十六年，孝惠章皇后崩，署內務府總管事務，大事將畢，乃罷。 五十七年，辦理正白旗滿洲、蒙古、漢軍三旗事。 六十年，上以御極六十年，遣允祹祭盛京三陵。 六十一年，授鑲黃旗滿洲都統。 世宗即位，進封履郡王。 雍正二年，宗人府劾允祹治事不能敬謹，請奪爵，命在固山貝子上行走。 二月，因聖祖配享儀注及封妃金冊遺漏舛錯，降鎮國公。 八年五月，复封郡王。 高宗即位，進封履親王。 乾隆二十八年七月，薨，予諡。
Prince Luyi of the First Rank Yunyou was Kangxi's twelfth son. In the tenth month of the forty-eighth year of the Kangxi reign he was enfeoffed as beizi. From then on he always accompanied the emperor whenever Kangxi went on tour. In the fifty-sixth year, when Empress Xiaohuizhang died, he served as acting commissioner of the Imperial Household Department and was relieved once the major funeral affairs were nearly complete. In the fifty-seventh year he managed the affairs of the Plain White Banner's Manchu, Mongol, and Chinese companies. In the sixtieth year, marking Kangxi's sixtieth year on the throne, Yunyou was dispatched to sacrifice at the three mausoleums of Shengjing. In the sixty-first year he was appointed lieutenant-general of the Bordered Yellow Banner Manchu. When the Yongzheng Emperor acceded he was promoted to Prince Lu of the second rank. In the second year of the Yongzheng reign the Imperial Clan Court impeached Yunyou for failing to manage affairs with due reverence and diligence and recommended stripping his title. He was ordered to serve at gushan beizi rank. In the second month, because of omissions and errors in the ritual regulations for Kangxi's posthumous enshrinement and the golden patent for ennobling a consort, he was reduced to prince of the state. In the fifth month of the eighth year he was again enfeoffed as prince of the second rank. When the Qianlong Emperor acceded he was promoted to Prince Lu of the first rank. In the seventh month of the twenty-eighth year of the Qianlong reign he died, and a posthumous title was granted.
79
子弘昆，先卒，用世子例殯葬，餘子皆未封。 高宗命以皇四子永為允祹後，襲郡王。 四十二年，薨，諡曰端。 嘉慶四年，追封親王。 子綿惠，襲貝勒。 嘉慶元年，薨，追封郡王。 以成郡王綿懃子奕綸為後，襲貝子，進貝勒。 子孫循例遞降，以鎮國公世襲。
His son Hongkun died first and was buried by the precedent for an heir apparent. None of his remaining sons were enfeoffed. The Qianlong Emperor ordered his fourth son Yonglin to become Yunyou's heir and succeed to the princedom of the second rank. In the forty-second year he died, and his posthumous title was Duan. In the fourth year of the Jiaqing reign he was posthumously enfeoffed as prince of the first rank. His son Mianhui succeeded as beile. In the first year of the Jiaqing reign he died and was posthumously enfeoffed as prince of the second rank. Yilun, son of Prince Cheng of the second rank Mianqin, was made heir. He succeeded as beizi and was later promoted to beile. Descendants successively declined by precedent, with the title of prince of the state passing in perpetual inheritance.
80
乾隆四十二年，高宗南巡，還蹕次涿州，有僧攜童子迎駕，自言永庶子，為側室福晉王氏所棄，僧育以長。 上問永嫡福晉伊爾根覺羅氏，言永子以痘殤。 乃令入都，命軍機大臣詰之。 童子端坐名諸大臣，諸大臣不敢決。 軍機章京保成直前批其頰，叱之，童子乃自承劉氏子，僧教為妄語。 斬僧，戍童子伊犁，仍自稱皇孫，所為多不法。 上命改戍黑龍江，道庫倫，庫倫辦事大臣松筠責其不法，縛出，絞殺之，高宗嘉其明決。
In the forty-second year of the Qianlong reign, during the Qianlong Emperor's southern tour, on the return halt at Zhuozhou a monk brought a boy to greet the imperial procession. The boy claimed to be Yonglin's son by a concubine, abandoned by secondary consort Wang and raised by the monk. The emperor questioned Yonglin's primary consort, née Irgen Gioro, who said Yonglin's son had died young of smallpox. The boy was therefore ordered to enter the capital, and the Grand Council ministers were commanded to interrogate him. The boy sat upright and called the senior ministers by name, and the ministers did not dare reach a decision. Grand Council clerk Baocheng stepped forward, slapped the boy's cheek, and rebuked him. The boy then admitted on his own that he was a Liu clansman's son and that the monk had coached him to lie. The monk was beheaded and the boy was banished to Ili. He continued to call himself an imperial grandson and behaved in many unlawful ways. The emperor ordered that he be banished to Heilongjiang instead. Passing through Khüree, Commissioner Songyun rebuked his misconduct, had him bound and taken out, and executed him by strangulation. The Qianlong Emperor praised Songyun's firm and decisive action.
81
怡賢親王允祥，聖祖第十三子。 康熙三十七年，從上謁陵。 自是有巡幸，輒從。 六十一年，世宗即位，封為怡親王。 尋命總理戶部三庫。 雍正元年，命總理戶部。 十一月，諭：「怡親王於皇考時敬謹廉潔，家計空乏，舉國皆知。 朕御極以來，一心翊戴，克盡臣弟之道。 從前兄弟分封，各得錢糧二十三萬兩，朕援此例賜之，奏辭不已，宣諭再四，僅受十三萬； 复援裕親王例，令支官物六年，王又固辭。 今不允所請，既不可； 允其請，而實心為國之懿親，轉不得與諸弟兄比，朕心不安。 」下諸王大臣議。 既，仍允王請，命王所兼管佐領俱為王一等一員、二等四員、三等十二員，豹尾槍二、長桿刀二，每佐領增親軍二名？ 屬，加護。 二年，允祥請除加色、加平諸弊，並增設三庫主事、庫大使，從之。
Prince Yixian of the First Rank Yunxiang was Kangxi's thirteenth son. In the thirty-seventh year of the Kangxi reign he accompanied the emperor to pay respects at the imperial mausoleums. From then on he always accompanied the emperor whenever Kangxi went on tour. In the sixty-first year, when the Yongzheng Emperor acceded, he was enfeoffed as Prince Yi of the first rank. Soon he was ordered to oversee the three treasuries of the Ministry of Revenue. In the first year of the Yongzheng reign he was ordered to oversee the Ministry of Revenue. In the eleventh month the Yongzheng Emperor proclaimed: "In my late father's time Prince Yi was reverent, diligent, and incorrupt. His household was destitute, and the whole realm knew it. Since I ascended the throne he has devoted himself to supporting me and fully lived up to his duties as both younger brother and subject. When my brothers were enfeoffed in the past each received 230,000 taels of stipend. I applied that precedent in granting to him, but he memorialized again and again refusing. After repeated proclamations he accepted only 130,000 taels; I also applied the precedent of Prince Yu, allowing him official supplies for six years, but the prince again steadfastly declined. If I now refuse his request, that will not do; yet if I grant his request, a kinsman who truly serves the state with all his heart will be unable to receive what my other brothers did, and that weighs on my conscience. " He submitted the matter to the princes and senior ministers for deliberation. Thereafter the prince's request was still granted. All companies under his joint management were assigned as his retainers, with enhanced guard ranks—one first-rank guard, four second-rank, twelve third-rank, two leopard-tail spears, two long-shafted blades, and two personal guards added to each company. They were assigned as retainers with enhanced guard protection. In the second year Yunxiang requested the abolition of surcharge and balance-padding abuses and the addition of director and warehouse superintendent posts in the three treasuries, and his request was approved.
82
三年二月，三年服滿。 以王總理事務謹慎忠誠，從優議敘，復加封郡王，任王於諸子？ 中指封。 八月，加俸銀萬。 京畿被水，命往勘。 十二月，令總理京畿水利。 疏言：「直隸河與汶河合流東下。 滄、景以下，春？ 河、淀河、子牙河、永定河皆匯於天津大直沽入海，河？ 多淺阻，伏秋暴漲，不免潰溢。 請將滄州磚河、青縣興濟河故道疏濬，築減水壩，以洩之漲； 並於白塘口入海處開直河，使磚河、興濟河同歸白塘出海； 又濬東、西二淀，多開引河，使脈絡相通，溝澮四達； 仍疏趙北、苑家二口以防衝決。 子牙河為滹沱及漳水下流，其下有清河、夾河、月河同趨於淀，宜開決分注，緩其奔放之勢。 永定河故道已湮，應自柳義水所歸，應逐年疏濬，使濁水不能為患。 ？ 口引之稍北，繞王慶坨東北入淀，至三角淀，為又請於京東灤、薊、天津，京南文、霸、任丘、新、雄諸州縣設營田專官，募農耕種。 」四年二月，疏言直隸興修水利，請分諸河為四局，下吏、工諸部議，議以南運河與臧家橋以下之子牙河、苑家口以東之淀河為一局，令天津道領之； 苑家口以西各淀池及畿南諸河為一局，以大名道改清河道領之； 永定河為一局，以永定分司改道領之； 北運河為一局，撤分司以通永道領之：分隸專官管轄。 尋又命分設京東、京西水利營田使各一。 三月，疏陳京東水利諸事。 五月，疏陳畿輔西南水利諸事。 皆下部議行。
In the second month of the third year the three-year mourning period ended. Because the prince had managed affairs with caution and steadfast loyalty, he was given preferential commendation, promoted again to prince of the second rank, and permitted to designate one of his sons for enfeoffment by pointing. He was permitted to designate an heir by pointing among his sons. In the eighth month he was granted an additional stipend of ten thousand taels of silver. When the capital region suffered flooding he was ordered to go and inspect the damage. In the twelfth month he was ordered to oversee water conservancy throughout the capital region. He memorialized: "The Wei River joins the Wen River and flows eastward. Below Cangzhou and Jingzhou, during the spring flood season, the Wei River, the Dian River, the Ziya River, and the Yongding River all gather at Dazhigu in Tianjin to enter the sea. The channels are largely shallow and obstructed, and when summer and autumn floods surge the banks inevitably overflow. He requested dredging the old channels of the Brick River at Cangzhou and the Xingji River at Qingxian and building spillway dams to discharge floodwaters; and opening a straight channel at the Baitang estuary so the Brick River and Xingji River could together reach the sea through Baitang; also dredging the eastern and western marshes, opening diversion channels so the waterways connected and drains reached in all directions; and still clearing the Zhao North and Yuanjia outlets to guard against breaches. The Ziya River carries the lower courses of the Hutuo and Zhang Rivers. Below it the Qing, Jia, and Yue rivers all trend toward the marshes, so outlets should be opened to divide the flow and slow its force. The Yongding River's old channel was already silted up. From Liuyi Kou the waters should be drawn and dredged year by year so muddy water could no longer become a hazard. The channel should be drawn slightly north from Liuyi Kou, circling northeast of Wangqingtuo to enter the marshes and reach Triangular Marsh, where all waters gather. He also requested special farm-colony officials in eastern Jingdong at Luan, Ji, and Tianjin and in southern Jingnan at Wen, Ba, Renqiu, Xin, and Xiong to recruit farmers for cultivation. " In the second month of the fourth year he memorialized on waterworks in Zhili and requested that the rivers be divided into four bureaus. The Ministries of Personnel and Works deliberated and decided that the Grand Canal south of Zangjia Bridge, the Ziya River below it, and the Dian River east of Yuanjiakou would form one bureau under the Tianjin intendant; the marshes west of Yuanjiakou and the southern capital-region rivers would form one bureau, led by the Daming intendant retitled Qinghe intendant; the Yongding River would form one bureau, led by the Yongding sub-commissioner promoted to intendant; and the Northern Grand Canal would form one bureau, with the sub-commissioner withdrawn and the Tongyong intendant placed in charge—each under a specialized official. Soon separate eastern Jingdong and western Jingxi water-conservancy and farm-colony commissioners were also appointed. In the third month he memorialized on waterworks affairs in eastern Jingdong. In the fifth month he memorialized on waterworks affairs in southwestern Jifu. All were submitted to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
83
七月，賜御書「忠敬誠直勤慎廉明」榜，諭曰：「怡親王事朕，克殫忠誠，職掌有九，而公爾忘私，視國如家，朕深知王德，覺此八字無一毫過量之詞。 在朝諸臣，於'忠勤慎明'尚多有之，若'敬誠直廉'，則未能輕許。 期咸砥礪，以副朕望。 」七年六月，命辦理西北兩路軍​​機。 十月，命增儀仗一倍。 十一月，王有疾。 八年五月，疾篤，上親臨視，及至，王已薨，上悲慟，輟朝三日。 翌日，上親臨奠，諭：「怡親王薨逝，中心悲慟，飲食無味，寢臥不安。 王事朕八年如一日，自古無此公忠體國之賢王，朕待王亦宜在常例之外。 今朕素服一月，諸臣常服，宴會俱不必行。 」越日，复諭舉怡親王功德，命復其名上一字為「胤」，配享太廟，諡曰賢，並以「忠敬誠直勤慎廉明」八字加於諡上。 白家甿等十三村民請建祠，允之。 撥官地三十餘頃為祭田，免租賦。 命更定園寢之制，視常例有加。 又命未殯，月賜祭； 小祥及殯，視大祭禮賜祭； 三年後，歲賜祭。 皆特恩，不為例。 乾隆中，祀盛京賢王祠。 命王爵世襲。
In the seventh month the Yongzheng Emperor bestowed an imperial inscription reading "Loyal, reverent, sincere, upright, diligent, cautious, incorrupt, and clear-sighted" and proclaimed: "Prince Yi serves me with complete loyalty. He holds nine offices yet forgets private interest for public duty and treats the state as his own household. I know the prince's character well and feel these eight words contain not a trace of excess praise. Among the ministers at court, many can still be found for 'loyal, diligent, cautious, and clear-sighted,' but for 'reverent, sincere, upright, and incorrupt' the title cannot lightly be granted. I expect all to refine themselves to fulfill my hopes. " In the sixth month of the seventh year he was ordered to manage military affairs on the northwestern and southwestern routes. In the tenth month he was ordered to double his ceremonial guard. In the eleventh month the prince fell ill. In the fifth month of the eighth year, when his illness turned grave, the Yongzheng Emperor came in person to visit him. By the time he arrived the prince had already died. The emperor grieved deeply and suspended court for three days. The next day the Yongzheng Emperor came in person to offer sacrifice and proclaimed: "Prince Yi has passed away. My heart grieves deeply; food has no flavor and sleep brings no rest. The prince served me for eight years as though each day were the first. Since antiquity there has never been such a worthy prince who served the state with public loyalty, and my treatment of him should also have gone beyond ordinary precedent. Now I shall wear plain mourning for one month. The ministers shall wear ordinary dress, and banquets need not be held. " The next day he again proclaimed the prince's merits and ordered the first character of his name restored to "Yin," enshrinement in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, a posthumous title of Xian, and the eight words "Loyal, reverent, sincere, upright, diligent, cautious, incorrupt, and clear-sighted" added to the posthumous title. Villagers of Baijiatuan and twelve other villages requested that a temple be built in his honor, and the request was granted. More than thirty qing of official land was allocated as sacrificial fields, exempt from rent and tax. The regulations for the princely tomb precinct were revised with additions beyond ordinary precedent. He also ordered that before burial monthly sacrifices be granted; at the small anniversary and burial, sacrifices be granted on the scale of the great sacrificial rites; after three years, annual sacrifices be granted. All were special favors and were not made precedent. During the Qianlong reign he was enshrined in the Worthy Princes Temple at Shengjing. The prince's title was ordered to pass in perpetual inheritance.
84
子弘曉，襲。 乾隆四十三年，薨，諡曰僖。 子永瑯，襲。 嘉慶四年，薨，諡曰恭。 孫奕勳，襲。 二十三年，薨，諡曰恪。 子載坊，襲。 明年，薨。 弟載垣，襲。 事宣宗，命在御大臣。 咸豐八年，賜紫禁城內肩？ 前大臣行走，受顧命。 文宗即位，歷左宗正、宗令、領侍輿。
His son Hongxiao succeeded. In the forty-third year of the Qianlong reign he died, and his posthumous title was Xi. His son Yonglang succeeded. In the fourth year of the Jiaqing reign he died, and his posthumous title was Gong. His grandson Yixun succeeded. In the twenty-third year he died, and his posthumous title was Ke. His son Zaifang succeeded. The next year he died. His younger brother Zaituan succeeded. Serving the Daoguang Emperor, he was ordered to serve as an imperial front-rank grand minister. In the eighth year of the Xianfeng reign he was granted the use of a shoulder sedan within the Forbidden City. He served as a front-rank grand minister and received the imperial deathbed testament. When the Xianfeng Emperor acceded he successively held the posts of Left Director of the Imperial Clan, Director of the Imperial Clan, and Chief Commandant of the Guard.
85
載垣與鄭王端華及端華弟肅順皆為上所倚，相結，權勢日張。 九年，命赴天津察視海防。 十年正月，萬壽節，賜杏黃色端罩。 七月，英吉利、法蘭西兩國兵至天津，命與兵部尚書穆廕以欽差大臣赴通州與英人議和。 時大學士桂良已於天津定議，上許英使額爾金至通州簽約，英使額爾金請入京師親遞國書，不許。 兵復進，上以和議未成，罷載垣欽差大臣。 未幾，扈上幸熱河。 及和議定，？ 臣請還京師，上猶豫未決。 十一年七月，文宗崩，穆宗即位，載垣等受遺詔輔政，與端華、景壽、肅順及軍機大臣穆廕、匡源、杜翰、焦祐瀛稱「贊襄政務王大臣」，擅政。 九月，上奉文宗喪還京師，詔罪狀載垣等，奪爵職，下王大臣按治，議殊死，賜自盡。 事詳肅順傳。 爵降為不入八分輔國公，並命不得以其子孫及親兄弟子承襲。 同治元年，以莊親王允祿四世孫載泰襲輔國公，收府第敕書。 三年七月，師克江寧，推恩還王爵。 九月，以寧郡王弘？ 四世孫鎮國公載敦襲怡親王，還敕書。 光緒十六年，薨，諡，奪爵，以先薨免罪。 弟之？ 曰端。 子溥靜，嗣。 二十六年八月，薨。 九月，坐縱芘拳匪啟子毓麒，襲。
Zaituan, together with Prince Zheng Duanhua and Duanhua's younger brother Sushun, were all favorites of the emperor. They formed a faction and their power grew daily. In the ninth year he was ordered to go to Tianjin to inspect coastal defenses. In the first month of the tenth year, on the Longevity Festival, he was bestowed an apricot-yellow formal surcoat. In the seventh month, when English and French troops reached Tianjin, he was ordered with Minister of War Muyin to go as imperial commissioners to Tongzhou to negotiate peace with the English. At that time Grand Secretary Guiliang had already settled terms at Tianjin. The emperor permitted the English envoy Elgin to come to Tongzhou to sign the treaty, but when Elgin requested to enter the capital to deliver the letter of credence in person the request was denied. The troops advanced again. Because the peace talks were not completed the emperor dismissed Zaituan as imperial commissioner. Before long he accompanied the emperor on the journey to Rehe. When the peace agreement was settled, the ministers requested return to the capital, but the emperor hesitated and had not decided. In the seventh month of the eleventh year the Xianfeng Emperor died and the Tongzhi Emperor acceded. Zaituan and the others received the deathbed testament to assist in government. Together with Duanhua, Jingshou, Sushun, and the Grand Council ministers Muyin, Kuang Yuan, Du Han, and Jiao Youying they styled themselves "Grand Ministers Assisting in Government" and monopolized power. In the ninth month, as the emperor accompanied the Xianfeng Emperor's funeral back to the capital, an edict proclaimed the crimes of Zaituan and the others, stripped their titles and offices, and submitted them to princes and ministers for investigation. Death by dismemberment was recommended and self-strangulation was granted. The affair is detailed in the biography of Sushun. The title was reduced to fuguo gong outside the eight privileges, and an order was issued that neither his descendants nor the sons of his close brothers might succeed. In the first year of the Tongzhi reign Zaitai, fourth-generation descendant of Prince Zhuang Yunlu, succeeded as fuguo gong, and the princely residence patent was confiscated. In the seventh month of the third year, when the army captured Jiangning, favor was extended and the princely title was restored. In the ninth month Zaidun, fourth-generation descendant of Prince Ning Hongjiao and prince of the state, succeeded as Prince Yi, and the patent was restored. In the sixteenth year of the Guangxu reign he died, and a posthumous title was granted. His posthumous title was Duan. His son Pujing succeeded. In the eighth month of the twenty-sixth year he died. In the ninth month he was posthumously stripped of his title for indulging and shielding the Boxer bandits and provoking hostilities. Because he had already died he was spared further punishment, and his younger brother's son Yugi succeeded to the title.
86
寧良郡王弘晈，允祥第四子。 世宗褒允祥功，加封郡王，任王於諸子中指封，允祥固辭不敢承。 及允祥薨，世宗乃封弘？ 寧郡王，世襲。 乾隆二十九年八月，薨，諡曰良。 子永福，仍循例襲貝勒。 四十七年九月，薨，諡恭恪。 子綿譽，仍襲貝勒。 子孫遞降，以鎮國公世襲。 載敦紹封怡親王，即以載泰襲鎮國公。
Prince Ningliang of the Second Rank Hongjiao was the fourth son of Yinxiang.
