The Yongzheng Emperor praised Yinxiang's service, promoted him again to prince of the second rank, and allowed him to designate one of his sons for enfeoffment by pointing among them. Yinxiang steadfastly declined and would not accept. When Yinxiang died, the Yongzheng Emperor enfeoffed Hongjiao as Prince Ning of the second rank, with hereditary succession. In the eighth month of the twenty-ninth year of the Qianlong reign he died and was posthumously styled Liang. His son Yongfu succeeded as beile according to the usual rule. In the ninth month of the forty-seventh year he died and was posthumously styled Gongke. His son Mianyu likewise succeeded as beile. Descendants declined in rank by successive generations, the title passing hereditarily as zhenguo gong. Zaidun was enfeoffed in succession as Prince Yi, while Zaitai succeeded as zhenguo gong.
87
允祥諸子：弘昌，初封貝子，進貝勒，坐事奪爵； 弘暾，未封早世，聘於富察氏，未婚守志，世宗愍之，命視貝勒例殯葬； 弘昑，亦用其例。
Yinxiang's sons: Hongchang was first enfeoffed as beizi, promoted to beile, and later stripped of his title for an offense; Hongdun died young without receiving a title; betrothed to a lady of the Fuca clan, she remained faithful though unmarried. The Yongzheng Emperor commiserated and ordered that he be buried according to the beile precedent; Hongqin was likewise buried according to that precedent.

恂勤郡王允禵，聖祖第十四子。 康熙四十八年，封貝子。 五十年，從上幸塞外。 自是輒從。 五十一年，賜銀四千兩。 五十七年，命為撫遠大將軍，討策妄阿喇布坦。 十二月，師行，上御太和殿授印，命用正黃旗纛。 五十八年四月，劾吏部侍郎色爾圖督兵餉失職，都統胡錫圖索詐騷擾，治其罪。 都統延信疏稱：「準噶爾與青海聯姻婭，大將軍領兵出口，必有諜告準酋者，不若暫緩前進。 」上命駐西寧。 五十九年正月，允禵移軍穆魯斯烏蘇，遣平逆將軍延信率師入西藏，令宗查布防西寧，訥爾素防古木。 時別立新胡必爾汗，遣兵送之入藏。 十月，延信擊敗準噶爾將策零敦多卜等於卜克河諸地。 六十年五月，允禵率師駐甘州，進萬？ 次吐魯番。 旋請於明年進兵。 閏六月，和爾博斯厄穆齊寨桑以厄魯特兵五百圍回民，回餘人乞援。 允禵以糧運艱阻，兵難久駐，若徙入內地，亦苦糧少地狹，哈密扎薩克額敏皆不能容，布隆吉爾、達里圖諸地又阻瀚海，請諭靖逆將軍富寧安相機援撫，從之。 十月，召來京，面授方略。 六十一年三月，還軍。
Prince Xunqin of the Second Rank Yinti was Kangxi's fourteenth son. In the forty-eighth year of the Kangxi reign he was enfeoffed as beizi. In the fiftieth year he accompanied the emperor on a journey beyond the passes. From then on he always accompanied the emperor on such journeys. In the fifty-first year he was granted four thousand taels of silver. In the fifty-seventh year he was appointed Grand General for the Pacification of the Distance to campaign against Tsewang Araptan. In the twelfth month the army set out. The emperor presided at the Hall of Supreme Harmony to confer the seal and ordered that the Plain Yellow Banner standard be used. In the fourth month of the fifty-eighth year he impeached Vice Minister of Personnel Sertu for dereliction in supervising troops and supplies and Commander Hu Xitu for extortion and harassment; both were punished. Commander Yanxin memorialized: "The Dzungars are allied by marriage with Qinghai. When the grand general leads troops beyond the frontier, spies will certainly inform the Dzungar chief. It would be better to pause the advance for the moment. " The emperor ordered the army to encamp at Xining. In the first month of the fifty-ninth year Yinti moved his army to Murusi Usu, dispatched General for the Pacification of Rebellion Yanxin to lead troops into Tibet, ordered Zongcha to defend Xining, and Ne'ersu to defend Gumu. At that time a new Qoshot Khan was installed and troops were dispatched to escort him into Tibet. In the tenth month Yanxin defeated the Dzungar generals Tsewang Donjub and others at various places along the Boke River. In the fifth month of the sixtieth year Yinti led his army to encamp at Ganzhou and advanced and then halted at Turfan. He soon requested permission to advance the army the following year. In the intercalary sixth month the zaisang of Korbos Emuqi besieged Hui communities with five hundred Oirat troops, and the survivors pleaded for relief. Yinti reported that grain transport was arduous and the army could not remain long on campaign. If the troops were moved into the interior they would still suffer from scarce provisions and cramped terrain; Hami's jasaq Emin could not accommodate them, and Bulungir, Dalitu, and other places were cut off by the desert. He asked that Grand General for the Pacification of Rebellion Funing'an be instructed to give aid and reassurance as circumstances allowed, and his request was approved. In the tenth month he was summoned to the capital, where the emperor personally instructed him in strategy. In the third month of the sixty-first year he returned to the army.
89
世宗即位，諭總理王大臣曰：「西路軍務，大將軍職任重大，但於皇考大事若不來京，恐於心不安，速行文大將軍王馳驛來京。 」允禵至，命留景陵待大祭。 雍正元年五月，諭曰：「允禵無知狂悖，氣傲心高，​​朕望其改悔，以便加恩。 今又恐其不能改，不及恩施，特進為郡王，慰我皇妣皇太后之心。 」三年三月，宗人府劾允禵前為大將軍，苦累兵丁，侵擾地方，糜費軍帑，請降授鎮國公，上命仍降貝子。 四年，諸王大臣劾，請正國法。 諭：「允禵止於糊塗狂妄，其奸詐陰險與允禩、允禟相去甚遠。 朕於諸人行事，知之甚悉，非獨於允禵有所偏徇。 今允禵居馬蘭峪，欲其瞻仰景陵，痛滌前非。 允禵不能悔悟，奸民蔡懷璽又造為聽，宜加禁錮，即與其子白起並錮於壽皇殿左右，寬以歲月，待其改悔。 ？ 大逆之言，搖惑」高宗即位，命釋之。 乾隆二年，封輔國公。 十二年六月，進貝勒。 十三年正月，進封恂郡王。 二十年六月，薨，予諡。
When the Yongzheng Emperor acceded he instructed the supervising princes and senior ministers: "The western campaign is a grave responsibility and the grand general's charge is weighty; yet if he does not come to the capital for my late father's funeral I fear I shall have no peace of mind. Send orders at once for the Grand General Prince to come post-haste to the capital. " When Yinti arrived he was ordered to remain at Jingling to await the great mourning rites. In the fifth month of the first year of the Yongzheng reign an edict proclaimed: "Yinti is ignorant, reckless, and insufferably proud; I still hope he will repent so that I may show him favor. Fearing now that he may not reform and not wishing to withhold grace entirely, I specially promote him to prince of the second rank to comfort my empress dowager mother. " In the third month of the third year the Imperial Clan Court impeached Yinti for his former conduct as grand general—overworking the troops, harassing the countryside, and wasting military funds—and asked that he be reduced to zhenguo gong. The emperor ordered that he be reduced only to beizi. In the fourth year the princes and senior ministers impeached him and asked that he be punished according to law. An edict proclaimed: "Yinti is merely muddled and arrogant; his treachery, deceit, and secret malice are far removed from those of Yunsi and Yuntang. I know the conduct of all these men very thoroughly and am not showing partiality toward Yinti alone. Now that Yinti dwells at Malanyu, I wish him to gaze upon Jingling and thoroughly cleanse himself of his former faults. Yinti could not repent. The villain Cai Huaixi again fabricated treasonous reports. Yinti should be placed under close confinement together with his son Bai Qi on either side of the Hall of Imperial Longevity, allowing time to pass while he was awaited to reform. words of great treason to sway and deceive the hearts of men?" When the Qianlong Emperor acceded he ordered Yinti's release. In the second year of the Qianlong reign he was enfeoffed as fuguo gong. In the sixth month of the twelfth year he was promoted to beile. In the first month of the thirteenth year he was promoted and enfeoffed as Prince Xun of the second rank. In the sixth month of the twentieth year he died and was granted a posthumous title.
90
第一子弘春，雍正元年，封貝子。 二年，坐允禩黨，革爵。 四年，封鎮國公。 六年，進貝子。 九年，進貝勒。 十一年，封泰郡王。 十二年八月，諭責弘春輕佻，复降貝子。 高宗即位，奪爵。 別封允禵第二子弘明為貝勒。 乾隆三十二年，卒，諡恭勤。 子孫循例遞降，以不入八分鎮國公世襲。 弘春曾孫奕山，自有傳。
His first son Hongchun was enfeoffed as beizi in the first year of the Yongzheng reign. In the second year his title was revoked for membership in Yunsi's faction. In the fourth year he was enfeoffed as zhenguo gong. In the sixth year he was promoted to beizi. In the ninth year he was promoted to beile. In the eleventh year he was enfeoffed as Prince Tai of the second rank. In the eighth month of the twelfth year an edict rebuked Hongchun for frivolity and again reduced him to beizi. When the Qianlong Emperor acceded his title was revoked. Yinti's second son Hongming was separately enfeoffed as beile. In the thirty-second year of the Qianlong reign he died and was posthumously styled Gongqin. Descendants declined in rank according to precedent, the title passing hereditarily as buru bafen zhenguo gong. Hongchun's great-grandson Yishan has a separate biography.
91
愉恪郡王允潖，聖祖第十五子。 康熙三十九年，從幸塞外。 自是輒從。 雍正四年，封貝勒。 命守景陵。 八年，封愉郡王。 九年二月，薨，予諡。 子弘慶，襲。 乾隆三十四年，薨，諡曰恭。 子永珔，襲貝勒。 子孫循例遞降，以輔國公世襲。
Prince Yukuo of the Second Rank Yunpeng was Kangxi's fifteenth son. In the thirty-ninth year of the Kangxi reign he accompanied the emperor on a journey beyond the passes. From then on he always accompanied the emperor on such journeys. In the fourth year of the Yongzheng reign he was enfeoffed as beile. He was ordered to guard Jingling. In the eighth year he was enfeoffed as Prince Yu of the second rank. In the second month of the ninth year he died and was granted a posthumous title. His son Hongqing succeeded. In the thirty-fourth year of the Qianlong reign he died and was posthumously styled Gong. His son Yongbing succeeded as beile. Descendants declined in rank according to precedent, the title passing hereditarily as fuguo gong.

果毅親王允禮，聖祖第十七子。 康熙四十四年，從幸塞外。 自是輒從。 雍正元年，封果郡王，管理藩院事。 三年，諭曰：「果郡王實心為國，操守清廉，宜給親王俸，護衞亦如之，班在順承郡王上。 」六年，進親王。 七年，命管工部事。 八年，命總理戶部三庫。 十一年，授宗令，管戶部。 十二年，命赴泰寧，送達賴喇嘛還西藏，循途巡閱諸省駐防及綠營兵。 十三年，還京師，命辦理苗疆事務。 世宗疾大漸，受遺詔輔政。
Prince Guoyi of the First Rank Yunli was Kangxi's seventeenth son. In the forty-fourth year of the Kangxi reign he accompanied the emperor on a journey beyond the passes. From then on he always accompanied the emperor on such journeys. In the first year of the Yongzheng reign he was enfeoffed as Prince Guo of the second rank and ordered to manage the Court of Colonial Affairs. In the third year an edict proclaimed: "Prince Guo serves the state with a sincere heart and maintains incorrupt conduct. He should receive a prince of the first rank's stipend, with guards to match, and rank above Prince Shuncheng of the second rank. " In the sixth year he was promoted to prince of the first rank. In the seventh year he was ordered to manage the Ministry of Works. In the eighth year he was ordered to oversee the three treasuries of the Ministry of Revenue. In the eleventh year he was appointed clan chancellor and placed in charge of the Ministry of Revenue. In the twelfth year he was ordered to go to Taining to escort the Dalai Lama back to Tibet and, along the route, to inspect provincial garrisons and Green Standard troops. In the thirteenth year he returned to the capital and was ordered to manage affairs on the Miao frontier. When the Yongzheng Emperor's illness grew critical he received the deathbed testament to assist in government.
93
高宗即位，命總理事務，解宗令，管刑部。 尋賜親王雙俸，免宴見叩拜。 密疏請蠲江南諸省民欠漕項、蘆課、學租、雜稅，允之。 諭曰：「果親王秉性忠直，皇考所信任。 外間頗疑其嚴厲，今觀密奏，足見其存心寬厚，特以宣示九卿。 」允禮體弱，上命在邸治事，越數日一入直。 乾隆元年，坐事，罷雙俸。 三年正月，病篤，遣和親王弘晝往視。 二月，薨，上震悼，即日親臨其喪。 予諡。 無子，莊親王允祿等請以世宗第六子弘曕爲之後。
When the Qianlong Emperor acceded he was ordered to oversee general affairs, relieved of the clan chancellorship, and placed in charge of the Ministry of Justice. He was soon granted a prince of the first rank's double stipend and exempted from bowing at banquets and audiences. In a secret memorial he requested remission of popular arrears in grain transport dues, reed levies, school rents, and miscellaneous taxes in the southern provinces, and his request was approved. An edict proclaimed: "Prince Guo is loyal and upright by nature, and my late father trusted him. Many outside court suspected him of severity, but reading this secret memorial one sees how generous his heart truly is. I therefore make it known to the Nine Ministers. " Yunli was weak in constitution. The emperor ordered him to conduct business at his residence, entering attendance only every few days. In the first year of the Qianlong reign, for an offense, his double stipend was revoked. In the first month of the third year, when his illness was grave, Prince He Hongzhou was dispatched to visit him. In the second month he died. The emperor was deeply grieved and that same day personally attended his funeral. A posthumous title was granted. He had no son. Prince Zhuang Yunlu and others requested that the Yongzheng Emperor's sixth son Hongyan be made his heir.
94
弘適善詩詞，雅好藏書，與怡府明善堂埒。 禦下嚴，晨起披衣巡視，遇不法者立杖之，故無敢為非者。 節儉善居積，嘗以開煤？ 奪民產。 從上南巡，囑兩淮鹽政高恒鬻人葠牟利，又令織造關差致繡段、玩器，予賤值。 二十八年，圓明園九州清宴災，弘適後至，與諸皇子談笑露齒，上不懌。 又嘗以門下私人囑阿里袞。 上發其罪，並責其奉母妃儉薄，降貝勒，罷一切差使。 自是家居閉門，意抑鬱不自聊。 三十年三月，病篤，上往撫視。 弘適於臥榻間叩首引咎，上執其手，痛曰：「以汝年少，故稍加拂拭，何愧恧若此？ 」因復封郡王。 旋薨，予諡。
Hongshi was skilled in poetry and dearly loved collecting books, rivaling the Mingshan Hall library of the Prince Yi residence. He was strict toward those below him. Each morning he rose, threw on his robe, and made the rounds of inspection; when he encountered wrongdoers he immediately had them beaten with the staff, so none dared misconduct themselves. Frugal and adept at accumulating wealth, he once opened coal mines and seized the people's property in doing so. On a southern tour with the emperor, he instructed the Liang-Huai salt commissioner Gao Heng to sell ginseng for profit, and also ordered the weaving-office agents to supply embroidered silks and curios while paying them at low prices. In the twenty-eighth year, when the Nine Provinces Serene Banquet at the Old Summer Palace burned, Hongshi arrived late. He laughed and talked with the other princes, baring his teeth, and the emperor was displeased. He also once entrusted a private retainer to Ali Geng. The emperor exposed his crimes and also rebuked him for treating his mother consort stingily. He was reduced to beile and removed from all appointments. From then on he lived at home behind closed doors, depressed and ill at ease. In the third month of the thirtieth year, when his illness was grave, the emperor went to visit and comfort him. Hongshi kowtowed on his sickbed and took blame upon himself. The emperor took his hand and said in anguish, "Because you are young, I merely sought to polish you a little—why such shame and embarrassment? " He then restored him as Prince of the Second Rank. He soon died and was granted a posthumous title.
95
子永瑹，襲。 五十四年，薨，諡曰簡。 子綿從，襲貝勒。 孫奕湘，襲鎮國公。 歷官副都統，廣州、盛京將軍，兵部尚書。 加貝子銜。 卒，諡恪慎。 子孫遞降，以輔國公世襲。
His son Yongshi succeeded. In the fifty-fourth year he died, and his posthumous title was Jian. His son Miancong succeeded as beile. His grandson Yixiang succeeded as Duke of the State Supporting the Nation. He held the posts of Deputy Lieutenant-General, Military Governor of Guangzhou and Mukden, and Minister of War. He was granted beizi rank. He died, and his posthumous title was Keshen. Descendants followed successive reduction in rank, with the title of Duke of the State Assisting the Nation passing in hereditary succession.
96
簡靖貝勒允禕，聖祖第二十子。 ，始從幸塞外，自是輒從。 雍正四年，封貝子。 八年二月，進貝勒。 十二年八月，命祭陵。 稱病不行，降輔國公。 十三年九月，高宗即位，复封貝勒，守護泰陵。 乾隆二十年，卒，予諡。 子弘閏，襲貝子。 子孫循例遞降，以不入八分鎮國公世襲。
Beile Jianjing Yunyi was Kangxi's twentieth son. He first accompanied the emperor beyond the passes and thereafter always went along. In the fourth year of the Yongzheng reign he was enfeoffed as beizi. In the second month of the eighth year he was promoted to beile. In the eighth month of the twelfth year he was ordered to perform mausoleum sacrifices. Claiming illness, he did not go and was reduced to fuguo gong. In the ninth month of the thirteenth year, when the Qianlong Emperor acceded, he was again enfeoffed as beile and ordered to guard Tailing. In the twentieth year of the Qianlong reign he died and was granted a posthumous title. His son Hongrun succeeded as beizi. Descendants followed the usual rule of successive reduction in rank, with the title passing hereditarily as buru bafen zhenguo gong.
97
慎靖郡王允禧，聖祖第二十一子。 康熙五十九年，始從幸塞外。 雍正八年二月，封貝子。 五月，諭以允禧立志向上，進貝勒。 十三年十一月，高宗即位，進慎郡王。 允禧詩清秀，尤工畫，遠希董源，近接文徵明，自署紫瓊道人。 乾隆二十三年五月，薨，予諡。
Prince Shenjing of the Second Rank Yunxi was Kangxi's twenty-first son. In the fifty-ninth year of the Kangxi reign he first accompanied the emperor on a journey beyond the passes. In the second month of the eighth year of the Yongzheng reign he was enfeoffed as beizi. In the fifth month an edict stated that because Yunxi was resolved to improve himself, he was promoted to beile. In the eleventh month of the thirteenth year, when the Qianlong Emperor acceded, he was promoted to Prince Shen of the Second Rank. Yunxi's poetry was refined and elegant. He was especially skilled at painting, looking back to Dong Yuan in the distant past and taking Wen Zhengming as his nearer model, and he styled himself the Daoist of Purple Jade. In the fifth month of the twenty-third year of the Qianlong reign he died and was granted a posthumous title.
98
二十四年十二月，以皇六子永瑢為之後，封貝勒。 三十七年，進封質郡王。 五十四年，再進親王。 永瑢亦工畫，濟美紫瓊，兼通天算。 五十五年，薨，諡曰莊。 子綿慶，襲郡王。 綿慶幼聰穎，年十三，侍高宗避暑山莊校射，中三矢，賜黃馬褂、三眼孔雀翎。 通音律。 體孱弱。 嘉慶九年，薨，年僅二十六。 仁宗深惜之，賜銀五千，諡曰恪。 子奕綺，襲貝勒。 道光五年，坐事，罰俸。 十九年，奪爵。 二十二年，卒，復其封。 子孫循例遞降，以鎮國公世襲。
In the twelfth month of the twenty-fourth year the sixth imperial son Yongrong was made his heir and enfeoffed as beile. In the thirty-seventh year he was promoted and enfeoffed as Prince Zhi of the Second Rank. In the fifty-fourth year he was again promoted to prince of the first rank. Yongrong was also skilled at painting, carrying on the Purple Jade tradition, and was likewise versed in astronomy and mathematics. In the fifty-fifth year he died, and his posthumous title was Zhuang. His son Mianqing succeeded as Prince of the Second Rank. Mianqing was clever from childhood. At thirteen, while attending the Qianlong Emperor at archery practice at the Mountain Resort for Escaping the Heat, he hit with three arrows and was granted a yellow riding jacket and a three-eyed peacock feather. He was versed in music. His constitution was frail. In the ninth year of the Jiaqing reign he died, aged only twenty-six. The Jiaqing Emperor deeply regretted his loss and granted five thousand taels of silver; his posthumous title was Ke. His son Yiqi succeeded as beile. In the fifth year of the Daoguang reign, for an offense, his salary was fined. In the nineteenth year his title was revoked. In the twenty-second year he died, and his title was restored. Descendants followed the usual rule of successive reduction in rank, with the title passing hereditarily as zhenguo gong.
99
恭勤貝勒允祜，聖祖第二十二子。 康熙五十九年，始從幸塞外。 雍正八年二月，封貝子。 十二年二月，進貝勒。 乾隆八年，卒，予諡。 子弘曨，襲貝子。 卒。 子永芝，襲鎮國公。 坐事，奪爵，爵除。
Beile Gongqin Yunhu was Kangxi's twenty-second son. In the fifty-ninth year of the Kangxi reign he first accompanied the emperor on a journey beyond the passes. In the second month of the eighth year of the Yongzheng reign he was enfeoffed as beizi. In the second month of the twelfth year he was promoted to beile. In the eighth year of the Qianlong reign he died and was granted a posthumous title. His son Honghuang succeeded as beizi. He died. His son Yongzhi succeeded as Duke of the State Supporting the Nation. For an offense his title was revoked and the peerage was extinguished.
100
郡王品級誠貝勒允祁，聖祖第二十三子。 雍正八年二月，封鎮國公。 十三年十月，高宗即位，進貝勒。 屢坐事，降鎮國公。 四十五年，复封貝子。 四十七年，進貝勒。 四十九年，加郡王銜。 五十年，卒，予諡。 子弘謙，襲貝子，嘉慶十四年，加貝勒品級。 卒，子永康，襲鎮國公。 卒，子綿英，襲不入八分鎮國公。 卒，無子，爵除。
Beile Cheng Yunqi, of princely rank, was Kangxi's twenty-third son. In the second month of the eighth year of the Yongzheng reign he was enfeoffed as zhenguo gong. In the tenth month of the thirteenth year, when the Qianlong Emperor acceded, he was promoted to beile. Repeatedly convicted in cases, he was reduced to zhenguo gong. In the forty-fifth year he was again enfeoffed as beizi. In the forty-seventh year he was promoted to beile. In the forty-ninth year he was granted princely rank. In the fiftieth year he died and was granted a posthumous title. His son Hongqian succeeded as beizi. In the fourteenth year of the Jiaqing reign he was granted beile rank. He died. His son Yongkang succeeded as Duke of the State Supporting the Nation. He died. His son Mianying succeeded as buru bafen zhenguo gong. He died without a son, and the peerage was extinguished.
101
諴恪親王允祕，聖祖第二十四子。 雍正十一年正月，諭曰：「朕幼弟允祕，秉心忠厚，賦性和平，素為皇考所鍾愛。 數年以來，在宮中讀書，學識亦漸增長，朕心嘉悅，封為諴親王。 」乾隆三十八年，薨，予諡。 第一子弘暢，襲郡王。 六十年，薨，諡曰密。 子永珠，襲貝勒。 道光中，坐事，奪爵。 弘？ ，允祕第二子，字仲升。 乾隆二十八年，封二等鎮國將軍。 三十九年，進封貝子。 屢坐事，奪爵。 嘉慶間，授奉恩將軍。 卒。 弘？ 工畫，師董邦達，自署瑤華道人，名與紫瓊並。 永珠既奪爵，以弘？ 孫綿勳襲貝子。 子孫遞降，以鎮國公世襲。
Prince Xianke Yunbi was Kangxi's twenty-fourth son. In the first month of the eleventh year of the Yongzheng reign an edict proclaimed: "My younger brother Yunbi is loyal at heart and gentle in nature, and has always been deeply loved by our late father. In recent years, studying in the palace, his learning has gradually increased. My heart is pleased, and I enfeoff him as Prince Xian of the First Rank. " In the thirty-eighth year of the Qianlong reign he died and was granted a posthumous title. His first son Hongchang succeeded as Prince of the Second Rank. In the sixtieth year he died, and his posthumous title was Mi. His son Yongzhu succeeded as beile. During the Daoguang reign, for an offense, his title was revoked. Hongwu Yunbi's second son Hongwu had the courtesy name Zhongsheng. In the twenty-eighth year of the Qianlong reign he was enfeoffed as second-rank zhenguo jiangjun. In the thirty-ninth year he was promoted and enfeoffed as beizi. Repeatedly convicted in cases, he was stripped of his title. During the Jiaqing reign he was appointed General by Grace. He died. Hongwu Hongwu was skilled at painting, studied under Dong Bangda, styled himself the Daoist of Jade Splendor, and his fame ranked with that of Purple Jade. After Yongzhu had been stripped of his title, Hongwu's grandson Mianxun succeeded as beizi. Descendants followed successive reduction in rank, with the title passing hereditarily as zhenguo gong.
102
世宗十子：孝敬憲皇后生端親王弘暉，孝聖憲皇后生高宗，純懿皇貴妃耿佳氏生和恭親王弘晝，敦肅皇貴妃年佳氏生福宜、懷親王福惠、福沛，謙妃劉氏生果恭郡王弘適，齊妃李氏生弘昀、弘時、弘昐。 弘適出為果毅親王允禮後。 弘昀、弘昐、福宜、福沛皆殤，無封。 弘時雍正五年以放縱不謹，削宗籍，無封。
The Yongzheng Emperor had ten sons. Empress Xiaojingxian gave birth to Prince Duan Honghui. Empress Xiaoshengxian gave birth to the future Qianlong Emperor. Imperial Noble Consort Chunyi, née Geng, gave birth to Prince Hegong Hongzhou. Imperial Noble Consort Dunsu, née Nian, gave birth to Fuyi, Prince Huai Fuhui, and Fupei. Consort Qian, née Liu, gave birth to Prince Guogong of the Second Rank Hongshi. Consort Qi, née Li, gave birth to Hongyun, Hongshi, and Hongfen. Hongshi was made heir to Prince Guoyi Yunli. Hongyun, Hongfen, Fuyi, and Fupei all died in infancy and received no enfeoffment. In the fifth year of the Yongzheng reign, Hongshi was expunged from the clan register for dissolute and careless conduct and received no enfeoffment.
103
端親王弘暉，世宗第一子。 八歲殤。 高宗即位，追封親王，諡曰​​端。
Prince Duan Honghui was the Yongzheng Emperor's first son. He died at the age of eight. When the Qianlong Emperor acceded he was posthumously enfeoffed as prince of the first rank, with the posthumous title Duan.
104
和恭親王弘晝，世宗第五子。 ，封和親王。 十三年，設辦理苗疆事務處，命高宗與弘晝領其事。 乾隆間，預議政。 弘晝少驕抗，上每優容之。 嘗監試八旗子弟於正大光明殿，日晡，弘晝請上退食，上未許。 弘晝遽曰：「上疑吾買囑士子耶？ 」明日，弘晝入謝，上曰：「使昨答一語，汝齏粉矣！ 」待之如初。 性復奢侈，世宗雍邸舊貲，上悉以賜之，故富於他王。 好言喪禮，言：「人無百年不死者，奚諱為？ 」嘗手訂喪儀，坐庭際，使家人祭奠哀泣，岸然飲啖以為樂。 作明器象鼎彝盤盂，置幾榻側。 三十年，薨，予諡。 子永璧，襲。 三十七年，薨，諡曰勤。 子綿倫，襲郡王。 三十九年，薨，諡曰謹。 弟綿循，襲。 嘉慶二十二年，薨，諡曰恪。 子奕亨，襲貝勒。 卒，子載容，襲貝子。 同治中，加貝勒銜。 卒，諡敏恪。 子溥廉，襲鎮國公。
Prince Hegong Hongzhou was the Yongzheng Emperor's fifth son. He was enfeoffed as Prince He of the First Rank. In the thirteenth year an office for handling Miao frontier affairs was established, and the Qianlong Emperor and Hongzhou were ordered to direct it. During the Qianlong reign he participated in deliberative government. Hongzhou had been arrogant and defiant since youth, and the emperor always treated him with forbearance. Once, while supervising the examination of Eight Banner youths in the Hall of Mental Cultivation, as dusk approached Hongzhou asked the emperor to withdraw for a meal. The emperor refused. Hongzhou suddenly blurted out: "Does Your Majesty suspect that I have bribed the candidates?" The next day Hongzhou came to apologize. The emperor said: "Had I answered you with a single word yesterday, you would have been ground to powder!" Yet he treated him as before. He was also extravagant by nature. The Yongzheng Emperor's old property from the Yong Prince's residence the emperor gave him in full, so he was wealthier than the other princes. He liked to speak of funeral rites, saying: "No one lives a hundred years without dying—why shrink from the subject?" He once edited mourning ritual by hand, sat at the edge of the courtyard, had his household offer sacrifice and weep in grief, and with stern composure ate and drank as though it were entertainment. He made spirit vessels in the form of tripods, ritual bronzes, plates, and bowls and placed them beside his couch and table. In the thirtieth year he died and was granted a posthumous title. His son Yongbi inherited the title. In the thirty-seventh year he died; his posthumous title was Qin. His son Mianlun inherited as Prince of the Second Rank. In the thirty-ninth year he died; his posthumous title was Jin. His younger brother Mianxun inherited the title. In the twenty-second year of the Jiaqing reign he died; his posthumous title was Ke. His son Yiheng inherited as beile. He died; his son Zairong inherited as beizi. During the Tongzhi reign he was granted the rank of beile. He died; his posthumous title was Minke. His son Pulian inherited as Duke of the State Supporting the Nation.
105
懷親王福惠，世宗第七子。 八歲殤。 高宗即位，追封親王，諡曰​​懷。
Prince Huai Fuhui was the Yongzheng Emperor's seventh son. He died at the age of eight. When the Qianlong Emperor acceded he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of the First Rank with the posthumous title Huai.
